### OAD-002 · Add the server-only SDK client, session cookies with refresh de-duplication and permissions ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-admin
- **Milestone:** M4
- **Depends on:** OAD-001, SDK-011
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/adr/0018-ota-admin-consumes-the-sdk-server-side.md (points 1–5, 10); ota/docs/adr/0011-console-access-staff-sessions-and-environments.md (points 4, 8, 9); ota/admin/README.md §4, §6 (`lib/`), §7, §8; docs/mvp/conventions.md §3
- **Files:** `ota/admin/src/lib/velexis.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/session.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/session.test.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/refresh-dedup.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/refresh-dedup.test.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/permissions.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/permissions.test.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/errors.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/errors.test.ts`, `ota/admin/src/lib/action-state.ts`, `ota/admin/package.json`
- **Steps:**
  1. Workspace dependency `@velexis/ota-sdk`. `lib/velexis.ts` (`import "server-only"`): `getConsole()` with React `cache`, building a server-mode client per request (`secretKey` = `OTA_ADMIN_SERVICE_KEY`, `baseUrl` = `OTA_API_URL`, staff `accessToken`, `sessionKind: "staff"`, `environment` from the session, `onResponse` logging one line without bodies, and `headers` with `X-Velexis-End-User-IP` (the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry, which Caddy sets, or `127.0.0.1` when there is none in local development) and `X-Velexis-End-User-Agent` (the browser's `User-Agent`, cut to 512 characters), read with `next/headers`, so the backend's sign-in throttle, lockout and `staff_actions` see the staff member's address, not the admin server's); `getStaff()` = `console.auth.me` once per request.
  2. `lib/session.ts`: read and write `__Host-vx_staff_at`, `__Host-vx_staff_rt`, `__Host-vx_env`, `__Host-vx_tenant` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`); `requireStaff(permission)` for server actions; redirect to `${PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL}/console?tenant=<id>` without a session.
  3. `lib/refresh-dedup.ts`: one in-process map from `sha256(refreshToken)` to the refresh promise and its result, kept 30 s, so parallel requests with the same old token get the same new tokens.
  4. `lib/permissions.ts` (`can(profile, permission)` from the scope matrix), `lib/errors.ts` (VelexisError code → message, `fieldErrors` → form state, `requestId` shown), `lib/action-state.ts`.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Two parallel refreshes with the same token make one SDK call and both receive the new tokens (unit test).
  - Every SDK request carries `X-Velexis-End-User-IP` taken from the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry and `X-Velexis-End-User-Agent`; a client-supplied left-most entry is never used (unit test with a fake `fetch`).
  - `can()` matches scope §1.3 for all five roles (table test); client components cannot import `lib/velexis.ts` (`server-only` build error asserted by a test fixture).
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin test && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin build`

### OAD-003 · Build the SSO, refresh and sign-out handlers and the middleware ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-admin
- **Milestone:** M4
- **Depends on:** OAD-002, OBE-059
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/admin/README.md §3 and §4; ota/docs/adr/0018-ota-admin-consumes-the-sdk-server-side.md (points 2, 3, 6); platform/docs/adr/0007-portal-to-ota-admin-sso-token.md (§5); docs/mvp/architecture.md §5 (c)
- **Files:** `ota/admin/src/app/sso/route.ts`, `ota/admin/src/app/sso/route.test.ts`, `ota/admin/src/app/auth/refresh/route.ts`, `ota/admin/src/app/auth/sign-out/route.ts`, `ota/admin/src/app/signed-out/page.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/middleware.ts`, `ota/admin/src/middleware.test.ts`, `ota/admin/next.config.ts`, `ota/admin/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. `POST /sso`: only `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `portalToken` matching `^ptk_[A-Za-z0-9]{24,64}$`; `Origin` must equal `PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL`; `console.auth.signIn({ grantType: "portal_token", portalToken })`; set the four cookies; `303 See Other` to `/bookings` (architecture flow (c), README §3 and PFE-019). Errors render a short page with "Back to the portal".
  2. `src/middleware.ts` (Node.js runtime; next to `src/app`, because Next.js ignores a `middleware.ts` at the app root when the app uses `src/`): refresh through the de-duplicated function when the access token expires within 60 s; redirect to the portal without a session; set the per-request CSP nonce header used by `next.config.ts`.
  3. `GET /auth/refresh?next=` (validated relative `next`) and `POST /auth/sign-out` (Origin checked, `console.auth.signOut`, clear cookies, `/signed-out`). A refused refresh clears the cookies and goes to the portal.
- **Acceptance:**
  - A foreign `Origin` on `/sso` answers 403; a token reused a second time shows the error page.
  - The SSO response sets four `__Host-` cookies with the attributes above and contains no token in the URL or body.
  - The middleware never refreshes the same token twice for parallel requests (test with two simultaneous requests).
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin test && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin build`

- **Files:** `tools/e2e/playwright.config.ts`, `tools/e2e/support/stack.ts`, `tools/e2e/support/ota.ts`, `tools/e2e/specs/ota-admin/sso-bookings.e2e.ts`, `tools/e2e/specs/ota-admin/pnr-import.e2e.ts`, `tools/e2e/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Add the Playwright project `ota-admin` (base URL `http://127.0.0.1:3002`, `testMatch` `specs/ota-admin/**/*.e2e.ts`); `support/stack.ts` also starts the built OTA admin when `E2E_WITH_OTA=1`.
  2. `sso-bookings.e2e.ts`: portal sign-in → "Open console" → `/bookings` of the right OTA; open a seeded manual-review booking → issue with a reason → status ticketed; cancel another with a full refund (airline-card booking, so no Stripe) → cancelled; reposting the captured SSO form fails.
  3. `pnr-import.e2e.ts`: import a PNR created in the stub for the tenant's office; the same for another tenant's office is refused.
  4. axe on every page visited (no serious or critical violation); `document.cookie` on the admin origin is empty for JavaScript.
- **Acceptance:**
  - The journeys pass locally and nightly, which meets the gate of platform task PFE-019 (OF-09).
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin build && E2E_WITH_OTA=1 pnpm test:e2e -- --project=ota-admin specs/ota-admin/sso-bookings.e2e.ts specs/ota-admin/pnr-import.e2e.ts`
- **Note:** 2026-10-30 (lead decision (1j), recorded by FIX-W34-OTA): for an airline-card booking, step 2's "cancel with a full refund" is the airline's void of the tickets issued today: the airline charged the traveller's card, so no money goes back through Velexis (`refund_via_airline`, the dialog offers "No refund from the console" alone), and the void reverses the airline's whole charge, which the journey checks as the payment's `airline.void_expected` event and no refund row (OADR-0004 and OADR-0018 point 8 over the plan text). Lead decision (2g) of the same day: the journey's `beforeAll` never books in the 3 minutes before midnight in the time zones that decide "today" (it waits until 00:00:05 of the new day, within its hook budget), so the cancel step's void of today's tickets never straddles midnight (tools/e2e/README.md, OTA admin journeys).

### OBE-078 · Receive Connect and per-connection Stripe webhooks ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M5
- **Depends on:** OBE-077, OBE-090
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/adr/0010-stripe-gateway-and-payment-webhooks.md (point 4); docs/mvp/architecture.md §5 (d) table; ota/docs/api-changes-console-and-internal.md §5
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/payments/webhooks/stripe-connect-webhook.controller.ts`, `ota/backend/src/payments/webhooks/stripe-connection-webhook.controller.ts`, `ota/backend/src/payments/webhooks/webhook-receiver.service.ts`, `ota/backend/src/config.ts`, `deploy/env/ota-backend.env.example`, `ota/backend/src/common/http/pending-operations.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/payments/connect-webhooks.int.test.ts`
- **Steps:**
  1. Config `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_CONNECT_TEST`, `_LIVE`. `/webhooks/stripe/connect/{environment}`: verify with the Connect secret; tenant **only** from `event.account` → `payment_provider_connections.account_reference` of a `connect_standard` connection.
  2. `/webhooks/stripe/c/{connectionId}`: verify with that connection's encrypted webhook secret; tenant **only** from the path's connection (`api_keys` mode).
  3. On both endpoints the OTA controls the Stripe account and can write any metadata, so metadata never selects the tenant: `metadata.velexis_tenant_id` and `metadata.velexis_environment`, when present, must equal the resolved tenant and environment; `event.livemode` must match the path's environment (Connect) or the connection's environment (`c/`); the payment is looked up only inside the resolved tenant and its `provider_payment_id` must match the event's object. Any mismatch is logged as a security event (no payload) and acknowledged with `200` without writing anything (OADR-0010 point 4).
  4. Both reuse the receiver of OBE-039 (store, acknowledge, enqueue, re-fetch with the right mode). Remove both from `pending-operations.ts`.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Signed fixtures for both endpoints are stored and processed once; a fixture signed with another connection's secret answers 400.
  - An event for an unknown `acct_` is acknowledged with 200 and ignored.
  - Forged metadata: a correctly signed Connect event from tenant A's account, and a `c/<ppc_id>` event of tenant A, each carrying `metadata.velexis_tenant_id` of tenant B, write no `payment_events` row in either schema, raise no staff alert and log a security event; a `livemode` mismatch behaves the same.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int payments`

- **Verify:** `E2E_WITH_OTA=1 pnpm test:e2e -- --project=storefront specs/storefront/live-and-domains.e2e.ts`
- **Note:** 2026-11-03 (lead decision (2j) of 2026-11-03, recorded by FIX-W40-OTA): step 2's "sign-in on the sub-domain redirects to the primary host" is the storefront's browser redirect of OFE-021 (`ota/frontend/src/lib/primary-host.js`: the sign-in and sign-up pages, from the sub-domain only, to the same path on the primary custom domain), which supersedes ADR-0018's 301 of the whole sub-domain for the MVP (its dated follow-up note). The previews run on the loopback address (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `tools/e2e/support/stack.ts`), a host that storefront.get does not list, where no redirect happens. So the journey shows it by mapping the sub-domain's host name to the preview with Chromium's host-resolver rules (`--host-resolver-rules` with a `MAP` rule for `<key>.ota.example.com`), opening the sign-in page on that host and asserting the navigation request to `https://<primary host>/account/sign-in.html`; it never needs the primary host to answer. A custom host serves the tenant without a redirect: only the sub-domain redirects, a custom domain never does (`StorefrontConfig.domains`). The browser still sends the mapped name as `Host`, and `vite preview` (Vite 6) answers a host name it does not allow with `403` "Blocked request" (`preview.allowedHosts`; loopback addresses and `*.localhost` pass by default), so the storefront would never boot there: the preview must allow `<key>.ota.example.com` (`ota/frontend/vite.config.js` or the preview's environment in `tools/e2e/support/stack.ts`, both outside this task's Files), or the journey answers that host's requests itself from the preview (`page.route` with `route.fetch` on the preview's address).

## M6 — Hardening & launch

Security review, the PCI controls of the airline-card flow and the gate for live airline-card payments, the erasure job, performance, runbooks, complete end-to-end suites and the SDK's first npm release. Foundation tasks X-029 … X-032 (monitoring, on-VM checks, restore drill, managed-services proof) run in the same milestone.

### OBE-087 · Add the 30-day customer erasure job ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-035, OBE-056
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/velexis-sdk/db/README.md §7 (deletion and erasure); ota/docs/data-model.md §6; ota/docs/scope.md §3.1 (`account.delete`)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/account/erasure.processor.ts`, `ota/backend/src/account/erasure.service.ts`, `ota/backend/src/account/erasure.service.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/jobs/schedulers.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/account/erasure.int.test.ts`
- **Steps:**
  1. `customers.erase` (daily) per tenant: customers soft-deleted more than 30 days ago are anonymised as db README §7 describes (identity, consents, sessions, saved data removed; bookings keep the financial record with traveller data anonymised where the law allows; `customer_id` detached).
  2. Idempotent and batched (100 customers per job); an audit `booking_events` or log entry per erasure without personal data.
- **Acceptance:**
  - A customer deleted 31 days ago (FakeClock) is anonymised; one deleted 29 days ago is untouched.
  - Bookings, payments and refunds keep their amounts and references after erasure.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test -- account && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int account`
- **Note:** 2026-11-05 (lead decisions (5f), (5g) and (5h) of 2026-11-05, carried out by FIX-W43-OTA): (5f) `customers.erase` runs hourly (minute 50, UTC; still per tenant, `active` and `suspended`, with this task's batches of 100, oldest deletion first, one transaction per customer) with a cut-off of 30 days less one hour: a customer whose `deleted_at` is at or before the job's instant less 30 days less one hour is erased, so the erasure always lands before `AccountDeletion.erasureDueBy` (deletion + 30 days; the `account.deleted` e-mail, OADR-0013 point 4), where the daily run could land up to a day after it; a customer deleted 29 days ago is untouched, one deleted 31 days ago is erased as before. (5g) The erasure also removes the recipient address, the variables and the subject of the customer's account e-mails in `notifications` (the `customer` templates: verification, password reset, address change, deletion; the rows stay with the placeholder recipient `erased@erased.invalid` and no personal data, a pending one is cancelled) and deletes the `checkout_travelers` and `checkout_contacts` of the customer's checkouts that never became bookings; bookings keep their travellers (db README §7). (5h) Each booking it detaches gets a `customer.erased` booking event (no actor, no data, staff only: step 2's audit entry, beside the log line), and auth.verifyEmail's `claimGuestBookings` skips the bookings that carry it, so a later verification of the erased customer's address never attaches them again. Proven by `erasure.service.test.ts`, `erasure.int.test.ts` (FakeClock: 29 days untouched, the cut-off and the next hourly run before `erasureDueBy`, no name, address or document ciphertext left in those tables, the marker) and `account.int.test.ts` (a new account verifying the address claims the ordinary guest booking only); [data model §6](../data-model.md#6-retention) and the dated note of the [flow](../flows/my-bookings-and-guest-lookup.md) §3.
- **Note:** 2026-11-05 (lead decisions (7a) and (7b) of 2026-11-05, second set, carried out by FIX-W44-OTA): (7b) the cut-off of `customers.erase` becomes 30 days less one hour and five minutes (`ERASURE_CUTOFF_AFTER_MS` = 30 days less one run interval and `ERASURE_MARGIN_MS`, `erasure.service.ts`), so the hourly run that first finds a customer due starts more than five minutes before `AccountDeletion.erasureDueBy`, and a run that starts late or works through a batch slowly still erases before it; a customer deleted 29 days ago is untouched, one deleted 31 days ago is erased as before. (7a) Of the customer's checkouts that never became bookings the erasure also deletes the `checkout_remarks` and sets `checkouts.ip_address` to NULL and `checkouts.metadata` to `{}` (the reference schema unchanged); a checkout that became a booking keeps them; the job's counts gain `checkoutRemarks` and `checkoutsCleared`. Proven by `erasure.service.test.ts` (the boundary, the first hourly run before `erasureDueBy` with five minutes to spare) and `erasure.int.test.ts` (FakeClock: 29 days untouched, the cut-off, the next hourly run, a next run almost five minutes late still before `erasureDueBy`; no special request, IP address or metadata value of the erased customer left in the checkouts that never became bookings; idempotent); [data model §6](../data-model.md#6-retention).

### OBE-092 · Cut the API's CPU per search so answers of 250 offers meet the search budget ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-028
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/performance.md §2 and §4; ota/docs/adr/0001-amadeus-client-design.md (point 9); ota/docs/adr/0002-offer-and-priced-offer-caching.md; ota/backend/test/load/README.md
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/amadeus/supplier-requests.repository.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/supplier-requests.repository.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/shopping/searches.service.ts`, `ota/backend/src/shopping/facets.ts`, `ota/backend/src/shopping/facets.test.ts`, `ota/docs/performance.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by OBE-028: with answers of 250 offers (what Amadeus answers at most, and what the API asks for unless a storefront sets a lower `maxResults`), the API spends about 150 ms of CPU per search, so 10 concurrent visitors queue on the event loop and the `flights.search` p95 without the stub delay is about 1 s (performance.md §2). Profile it again (`search-load.mjs --offers 250`, the API under the inspector or `--cpu-prof`) and confirm the shares of performance.md §2: the `supplier_requests` copy of the answer (the redactor and the contact masking walk the whole answer before the row is cut to 64 KB), facets and highlights, `decimal.js` in pricing and facets, the database driver for the 250-row insert, garbage collection.
  2. Cut the largest shares without changing what any operation answers or stores in the offer tables: for example build the stored copy of a search answer from no more of it than the 64 KB row keeps, so the redactor runs on less (it still runs on everything stored, OADR-0001 point 9), and compute facets and highlights with fewer `Decimal` objects. Add unit tests for every new path.
  3. Run the load test again with `--offers 250` and record the run and the profile in performance.md.
- **Acceptance:**
  - With `--visitors 10 --searches 200 --offers 250`, the p95 of `flights.search` without the stub delay is below 500 ms, or performance.md records why not and the decision it needs (a lower default `maxResults`, a worker thread, a second API process).
  - Every stored `supplier_requests` body is still redacted and cut to 64 KB (the repository's redaction tests pass unchanged), and the search and price integration tests pass unchanged.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test supplier-requests facets && node ota/backend/test/load/search-load.mjs --visitors 10 --searches 200 --offers 250`

### OBE-097 · Answer CORS for browsers that call the API with a publishable key ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-084
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/decisions.md §4 and §5 (third-party frontends use publishable keys plus bearer tokens); ota/backend/src/tenancy/api-key.verifier.ts (the publishable key's allowed origins, `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`); ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md §2.2 to §2.4 (the dated CORS note and its stand-in); the OTA OpenAPI document's `info.description` and its README §6; the SDK's transport (`ota/sdk`: the headers it sends); deploy/caddy/Caddyfile (the `api.ota` site block) and deploy/caddy/test/caddy-smoke.sh
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/main.ts`, `ota/backend/src/common/http/cors.ts`, `ota/backend/src/common/http/cors.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/m6/cors.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/openapi/velexis-ota-booking-api.openapi.yaml`, `ota/backend/openapi/README.md`, `deploy/caddy/Caddyfile`, `deploy/caddy/test/caddy-smoke.sh`, `ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by the lead (decision (15h) of 2026-11-11, from OFE-025): the OTA API answers no CORS today (preflight `OPTIONS` gets 404 without `Access-Control-*`), so a browser on another origin cannot call `api.ota.example.com` with a `pk_` key, although decisions §5 and the guide assume it can. Contract first: `info.description` says how the API answers CORS; change-log row.
  2. A preflight `OPTIONS` on any path answers 204 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoing the `Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` with every header the SDK sends (at least `X-Api-Key`, `Authorization`, `X-Booking-Token`, `Idempotency-Key`, `If-Match`, `Content-Type`, `Accept-Language`, `X-Currency`), `Access-Control-Max-Age` and `Vary: Origin`; never `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. A preflight carries no key, so it reveals nothing.
  3. An actual answer to a caller whose publishable key lists the request's `Origin` carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with that origin, `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` `X-Request-Id`, `Retry-After` and `ETag`, and `Vary: Origin`; secret keys, requests without an `Origin`, and origins the key does not list get none (an unlisted origin still answers `403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`). The hosted storefront's same-origin `/api/*` answers do not change.
  4. Caddy passes `OPTIONS` on `api.ota` through to the API (smoke test). Run the guide's browser samples again without the stand-in, remove the guide's dated CORS note and its pointers, and say so in the backend README.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Integration tests prove the preflight answer, the headers on an allowed origin, none on an unlisted origin (403 kept), a secret key and a request without `Origin`, and no `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` anywhere.
  - The guide's browser samples run from another origin against the local stack without a stand-in.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test cors && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int cors`
- **Note:** 2026-11-12 (lead decision (19d) of 2026-11-12, recorded by FIX-W50-OTA): since FIX-W49-OTA (lead decision (17e) of 2026-11-11), `Vary: Origin` goes on every answer of the API except the storefront edge's, requests without an `Origin` included, and no longer only on the preflights and on the answers opened to an origin the key lists. The "none" of step 3 and of the first acceptance criterion (secret keys, requests without an `Origin`, origins the key does not list) means no `Access-Control-*` header: those answers still carry `Vary: Origin`, as do a refused key's answers, the answers given before the key is checked (the body parsers' refusals, the router's `404`, the `400` of a path Express cannot decode) and a cacheable answer whose handler sets its own `Vary` (`Accept-Language`, `X-Api-Key`), because an answer given to a server without an `Origin` must not be reused for a page either (the Fetch standard's CORS and HTTP caches). The edge's answers (same origin, never opened) do not vary by `Origin`. `corsMiddleware` and `varyByOrigin` of `ota/backend/src/common/http/cors.ts` (and `error.filter.ts` for the undecodable path) set it, `cors.test.ts` and `cors.int.test.ts` prove it (`[FIX-W49-OTA AC1]`), and the contract's `info.description` (**Browsers on other origins (CORS)**) and `build-your-own-frontend.md` §2.4 say so.
- **Note (2026-11-23, KI-034, lead decision (39u) of 2026-11-23, approved by the owner; FIX-W70-API):** step 3 and the first acceptance criterion no longer hold for an origin the key does not list: its `403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` now carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with that origin (a serialized origin only; `null` gets none), the exposed headers and `Vary: Origin`, so that a browser page reads the refusal and the SDK raises `PermissionError` `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` after one request instead of `ConnectionError` `NETWORK_ERROR` after its retries. A publishable key is public, and the answer says only that this origin is not one of the key's. Secret keys, requests without an `Origin`, preflights, the edge and every other refusal of the credential (`401 INVALID_API_KEY` for an unknown, revoked or expired key from any origin, the `503` of a failed lookup) are unchanged. `allowCorsRefusal` of `ota/backend/src/common/http/cors.ts`, called by `CallerGuard`, sets the headers; `cors.test.ts`, `api-key.verifier.test.ts` and `cors.int.test.ts` prove it (`[FIX-W70-API AC4]`, which replace the unlisted-origin case of the `[OBE-097 AC1]` tests), and the contract's `info.description`, the backend README and `build-your-own-frontend.md` §2.4 say so. This Note changes no Status.

Contract first: `StorefrontSettings` gains the section `search` with `maxResults` (an integer from 1 to 250, or `null` for the API's default, whose value its description names) and `StorefrontSettingsUpdate` accepts it (absent: unchanged); `search` is not in `StorefrontSettings`' `required` list, so the OTA admin's typed fixtures (OAD-021's files) stay valid; change-log row, `pnpm contracts:lint`, `pnpm contracts:generate`, and the section in api-changes-console-and-internal.md §2.3.

A value outside 1–250 answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `path` `/body/search/maxResults`. - **Verify:** `pnpm contracts:lint && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test storefront-settings && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend exec vitest run --config vitest.int.config.ts test/integration/settings/storefront-settings.int.test.ts test/integration/shopping/search.int.test.ts`
- **Note:** 2026-11-12 (lead decision (19f) of 2026-11-12, recorded by FIX-W50-OTA): the `path` of step 2's `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` is `/search/maxResults`, a plain JSON pointer into the body, not `/body/search/maxResults`: only parameters get their location as a prefix (`/<in>/<name>`, `toFieldErrors` of `ota/backend/src/common/http/openapi-validation.interceptor.ts`), and the OTA document's `FieldError.path` is a JSON pointer into the request. That is what the API answers and what `storefront-settings.int.test.ts` (`[OBE-098 AC1]`, a value outside 1 to 250) and `console-settings.contract.test.ts` prove. OAD-021, whose settings page shows this error at the field, corrects its own block's step 2 the same way.

- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W48-SHARED (lead decision (15l) of 2026-11-11), OADR-0003's follow-up: a booking the reconciliation hands to the staff (`pending`, `reconcile_outcome = manual_review`, its checkout locked and its authorisation or airline-card payment held) cannot be closed in the OTA admin today: issue, cancel and resync refuse `pending` (`withoutOrderOf`), and no console operation releases an authorisation, so each such booking stays in the Reconciliation review view and goes to Velexis ops (supplier-timeout-and-reconciliation.md §4.3, "Known limitation"; launch checklist D3). Contract first: `consoleCloseBookingReview` (`POST /v1/console/bookings/{bookingId}/review-closure`, `x-sdk-method: console.bookings.closeReview`, `x-permission: bookings:cancel`, the staff who already cancel bookings and release their payments; `Idempotency-Key` required and `If-Match` as the other booking actions) with one of two outcomes: `order_found` with the order's `recordLocator`, or `not_booked` with a `note`. It answers the updated `ConsoleBookingDetails`, and `409 CONFLICT` with `details.reason` `not_in_review` (the booking is not in review) or `remark_mismatch` (the order's remark does not name this booking), or `ORDER_ALREADY_IMPORTED` as console.bookings.import answers. `ConsoleBookingActions` gains `canCloseReview`, not in its `required` list so that the OTA admin's typed fixtures (OAD-022's files) stay valid, with its reason in `reasons`. Change-log row, `pnpm contracts:generate`, the operation in api-changes-console-and-internal.md (§6's counts), the SDK route table and the contract test's assertions regenerated (`pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk generate`), the SDK method added to the console namespace with its route test, and, because the contract files are never edited (ADR-0019), the method listed in `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md` with the parity test's method count (128 → 129) and the SDK README's method count updated.
  2. `order_found`: read the order by its record locator in the booking's office (PNR import's by-reference read, with no transaction open during the Amadeus call) and accept it only with the remark `VELEXIS {reference}` of subtype BACKOFFICE of this booking, as the reconciliation does; then record it through the reconciliation's found path (`order-recorder.ts`: the order, its travellers and segments, the booking `confirmed`, `reconcile_outcome = found`, the checkout's lock released), so capture and ticketing follow as after an automatic find: a Stripe authorisation captured by the payments job, an airline-card order ticketed, or recorded as ticketed, as its ticketing policy says.
  3. `not_booked`: the booking becomes `failed` (`failure_code = SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT`, `reconcile_outcome = not_found`) as in the reconciler's not-found branch: a Stripe authorisation is voided through the `payment.void` job on the account that created it, the checkout is released (reopened if it has not expired) and the traveller gets `booking.not_confirmed`; an airline-card booking has nothing to void, and its note records that the agent asks the airline about a charge (never a card value). Lock order checkout, booking, payment; Flight Create Orders is never sent.
  4. Both outcomes write the staff event `booking.reconcile_closed` (the outcome and the staff member; no personal data but the record locator) and a `staff_actions` row; `canCloseReview` in the booking's actions (console-bookings.mapper.ts) says when the action is offered. Update OADR-0003's follow-up (dated: built), supplier-timeout-and-reconciliation.md §4.3 (the steps with the action, the limitation and its escalation row removed), launch-checklist.md D3 (the accepted limitation removed) and the backend README.
  5. Tests: unit tests of the outcome rules and `canCloseReview`; integration (the Amadeus stub and the fake Stripe API, `tenant_alpha` and `tenant_beta`): each outcome for a Stripe booking and an airline-card booking in review, from the request to the captured or voided payment, the booking's status, `reconcile_outcome`, the event, the `staff_actions` row and the e-mail; the refusals of step 1 and of a caller without `bookings:cancel`, each without a change; a replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the first answer, a new key `409 not_in_review`; a booking of another tenant answers `404`.
- **Acceptance:**
  - A booking in Reconciliation review closes as `order_found` (its order recorded, a Stripe authorisation captured, ticketing under way) or as `not_booked` (`failed`, a Stripe authorisation voided, the traveller e-mailed); either way its checkout's lock is released and `reconcile_outcome`, a staff event and a `staff_actions` row are written.
  - A booking not in review, an order whose remark names another booking or that another booking holds, a caller without `bookings:cancel` and another tenant's booking are refused without a change; the runbook and the launch checklist no longer record the limitation.
- **Verify:** `pnpm contracts:lint && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test review-closure console-bookings.mapper && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend exec vitest run --config vitest.int.config.ts test/integration/console/review-closure.int.test.ts test/integration/bookings/reconcile.int.test.ts && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test`

### OBE-100 · Add the OTA backend's secrets:rewrap command ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** X-040, OBE-007, OBE-036
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/adr/0010-secrets-envelope-encryption.md ("Rotation", item 3); docs/mvp/runbooks/master-key-rotation.md §1 and §3 (steps 5 and 7); packages/crypto/README.md ("KEK rotation", `rewrapBatch`); ota/backend/src/cli.ts (the command registry) and payments/airline-card/scrub-card-copies.command.ts (a command that walks every tenant schema); ota/backend/migrations/tenant/0001_baseline.sql (every `*_ciphertext` column with its `encryption_key_id`); ota/backend/src/checkout/traveler-documents.ts, notifications/outbox.repository.ts and common/http/idempotency.repository.ts (the writers and their associated data); platform/docs/plans/agent-tasks.md (PBE-072, the platform's command, for the shared output)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/cli.ts`, `ota/backend/src/cli.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/secrets/rewrap.command.ts`, `ota/backend/src/secrets/rewrap.repository.ts`, `ota/backend/src/secrets/rewrap.command.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/secrets/rewrap.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/README.md`, `docs/mvp/runbooks/master-key-rotation.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W48-SHARED (lead decision (15m) of 2026-11-11): ADR-0010 ("Rotation", item 3) and X-040 leave each backend's re-wrap command to its plan, and without it a master-key rotation can never remove the old key (master-key-rotation.md steps 5, 7 and 8; platform-operations.md §10 item 2). `secrets:rewrap [--tenant <key> | --all] [--dry-run] [--batch-size <n>]` (default `--all`): for every tenant schema, through `tenantTx`, one `rewrapBatch` row source per ciphertext column set of the tenant baseline, with the associated data its writer uses: `checkout_travelers` and `booking_travelers` (documents and discount eligibility), `notifications` (secret payload), `idempotency_keys` (response), and `saved_travelers` and `saved_traveler_documents`, which no MVP writer fills yet, so a later writer is covered; a row's ciphertexts that share one data key move together. `booking_documents.encryption_key_id` stays out while no writer sets it (the README says so).
  2. Output per tenant and table, then a total: rows re-wrapped, skipped and failed, and the count per KEK id (`remainingByKekId`) before and after; `--dry-run` reports the counts before and what would move, and writes nothing. Exit codes as PBE-072's: 0 when nothing is left under an old KEK, 1 when a row failed or remains, 2 for a usage error. It never prints or logs a row id, a ciphertext, a plaintext or a document number (counts and KEK ids only), and refuses to start when the current KEK cannot be loaded. The Amadeus token cache stays the runbook's flush (step 6).
  3. Tests: unit tests of the arguments and the report; integration on a `@velexis/testing` database with `tenant_alpha` and `tenant_beta` and values under `local:v1` and `local:v2` in every table: a run moves every value to the current KEK and a second run reports `rewrapped 0` and an empty `remainingByKekId` (idempotent); `--tenant` changes one schema only; `--dry-run` changes nothing; a corrupted ciphertext counts as failed and stays, a row changed between the read and the write is skipped; every value still decrypts with its associated data afterwards; the captured output and logs hold no plaintext, ciphertext or row id.
  4. master-key-rotation.md §1 and steps 5 and 7 (the OTA command's options and output) and the backend README's CLI table.
- **Acceptance:**
  - `node dist/cli.js secrets:rewrap` moves every ciphertext of every tenant schema to the current KEK, is idempotent, reports per tenant and table the counts per KEK before and after, and `--dry-run` writes nothing.
  - No output, log line or error of the command holds a secret, a ciphertext, a document number or a row id.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test cli rewrap && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend exec vitest run --config vitest.int.config.ts test/integration/secrets/rewrap.int.test.ts`

### OBE-101 · Keep Redis within its budget as tenants grow: bound the completed jobs the OTA worker keeps ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-088
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/performance.md §6 (item 4) and §7; docs/mvp/adr/0009-background-jobs-bullmq.md (item 7); ota/docs/adr/0014-per-tenant-workers-and-schedulers.md (points 1 and 7); docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md §5 (Redis) and §14; ota/backend/src/common/queues/queue-names.ts (`KEEP_COMPLETED_JOBS`, `DEFAULT_JOB_OPTIONS`, `otaWorkerOptions`); ota/backend/src/jobs/fan-out.ts; ota/backend/test/load/README.md (booking-load.mjs)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/common/queues/queue-names.ts`, `ota/backend/src/common/queues/queue-names.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/jobs/fan-out.ts`, `ota/backend/src/jobs/fan-out.test.ts`, `docs/mvp/adr/0009-background-jobs-bullmq.md`, `docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md`, `ota/docs/performance.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by OBE-088 (performance.md §6 item 4): every job the OTA worker completes stays in Redis for a day (`KEEP_COMPLETED_JOBS`, ADR-0009 item 7), 1 304 to 1 400 bytes for each job of the schedules, and the schedulers give each active tenant about 5 260 jobs a day (three schedules run every minute), about 7 MiB a day. So the completed jobs of about 60 active tenants fill Redis's `maxmemory` of 512 MiB, where `noeviction` then refuses BullMQ's writes, against the ~300 tenants of deployment §14. Propose the bound to the lead first, for example: the completed per-tenant scheduled jobs of `ota-maintenance` kept for an hour, the other queues' as they are, failed jobs 30 days as now. The bound must keep the deduplication that deterministic job ids get from the completed jobs. A fan-out iteration that is retried builds the same per-tenant ids, and BullMQ ignores an id it still holds (`fan-out.ts`); the iteration's backoffs add up to 7.5 minutes. Other producers use fixed ids too: the Stripe event ids, the payments' and the notifications' wake jobs. A bound by count, such as the last 1 000 jobs of `ota-maintenance`, keeps less than those 7.5 minutes once about 35 tenants are active. It needs a dated revision of ADR-0009 item 7.
  2. Apply the decided bound where the worker's options and the fan-out's job options are set, with unit tests; keep what the platform admin's failed-job view, `/health/ready` and the on-VM check read.
  3. Run `booking-load.mjs` with the bound, record in performance.md the bytes per job and what a day of completed jobs holds per tenant, and update the Redis line of deployment §14.
- **Acceptance:**
  - What a day of completed jobs holds in Redis no longer grows with the active tenants beyond the bound, measured with `booking-load.mjs` and recorded in performance.md.
  - Failed jobs are still kept 30 days, and the queue and fan-out unit tests pass.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test queue-names fan-out && node ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs --tenants 5 --minutes 10`

### OBE-102 · Keep a share of the Amadeus buckets free for shopping while the booking sync runs ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-018, OBE-045, OBE-088
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/performance.md §3 (why the buckets are 20 a second per credential set and 5 a second, burst 10, per tenant) and §6 item 2 (the four `429 RATE_LIMITED` answers to shoppers in the minutes of the sync's largest bursts); ota/docs/adr/0001-amadeus-client-design.md (point 6); docs/mvp/adr/0012-amadeus-account-model.md (the shared account's quota); ota/backend/src/amadeus/rate-limiter.ts (`TAKE_TOKENS_SCRIPT`, both buckets in one Lua script), limits.ts (the bucket constants), call-context.ts and amadeus.client.ts (where a call takes its tokens); ota/backend/src/bookings/booking-sync.service.ts and booking-sync.processor.ts (the sync's order reads, at most 20 per tenant a scan, the queue's 4 workers); ota/backend/test/load/README.md (booking-load.mjs)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/amadeus/rate-limiter.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/rate-limiter.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/limits.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/call-context.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/amadeus.client.ts`, `ota/backend/src/amadeus/amadeus.client.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/bookings/booking-sync.service.ts`, `ota/backend/src/bookings/booking-sync.service.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/amadeus/client.int.test.ts`, `ota/docs/adr/0001-amadeus-client-design.md`, `ota/docs/performance.md`, `ota/backend/test/load/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W49-SHARED (lead decision (17g) of 2026-11-11, approved by the owner): the booking sync's order reads take their tokens from the same buckets as the storefront's searches and prices, the tenant's (5 a second, burst 10) and the shared account's (20 a second for every OTA on it), so a sync burst (up to 20 bookings per tenant at one scan, about 12 reads a second from the queue's 4 workers) takes them from every OTA's shoppers: OBE-088 saw all four storefront `429`s of its run in sync bursts (performance.md §6 item 2). Propose the share first in a dated revision of OADR-0001 point 6, for example: a call of a background job that can wait (the sync's order reads; the task says which other job calls, if any, belong there) takes a token only while each bucket keeps at least a reserved share of its burst, half of it for instance, for the calls a person waits for (shopping, checkout, console), which still use the whole bucket; ticketing, the reconciliation of a lost answer and payments keep today's rule, because a delay costs a traveller there. A refused background call answers as today (`429` with the wait), and the sync job waits and retries as it already does after a `429`, without a failed booking.
  2. Implement the decided share: the call context says whether a call is background (`priority` or a set of operations, not a free value from a request), the rate limiter's script checks both buckets with the reserve in the same atomic step and takes nothing from either when one refuses, and the constants live in `limits.ts` with the reason. Unit tests of the script's arithmetic (a background call refused at the reserve and an interactive one let through, both buckets, refill), of the client passing the priority, and of the sync marking its calls; the client's integration test with Redis.
  3. Measure with `booking-load.mjs` (the run of performance.md §6: five tenants, the sync fixture, under `flock /home/user/wt/e2e.lock` with a scratch database and a private Redis, `nproc` and the load average beside every figure): the storefront's `429` answers in the minutes of the sync bursts before and after, the sync's own `429`s and how long its scans now take, and that the queue latency of `ota-bookings` stays within the 60 s of the plan. Record the run in performance.md (§6 item 2 and §7) and the load test's README.
- **Acceptance:**
  - A background call of the booking sync gets an Amadeus token only while the tenant's and the shared account's buckets keep the reserved share free, and the storefront's and the console's calls still use the whole bucket; both buckets change together or not at all (unit and integration tests).
  - `booking-load.mjs` shows fewer storefront `429` answers in the sync bursts than OBE-088's run, no booking failed by the sync's waits, and an `ota-bookings` queue latency within 60 s, recorded in performance.md with the dated revision of OADR-0001 point 6.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test rate-limiter amadeus.client booking-sync && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend exec vitest run --config vitest.int.config.ts test/integration/amadeus/client.int.test.ts && node ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs --tenants 5 --minutes 10`

### SDK-015 · Publish @velexis/ota-sdk 1.0.0 to npm
- **Status:** in progress (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7; pending: the owner's licence choice (H-14) and approval of the draft's lines (`ota/sdk/release/sdk-publish.draft.yml`, which then moves unchanged to `.github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml`), the npm organisation, `main` protected and the integration branch merged into it (about 4 December 2026), the trusted publisher (or the fallback token), the release commit with the repository field, the tag and the publish with provenance, by about 18 December 2026 and before January 2027)
- **Component:** ota-sdk
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** SDK-014, OBE-084
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/adr/0016-sdk-packaging-and-type-contract.md (points 7, 8); ota/sdk/README.md §9; ota/sdk/docs/types-and-builds.md §6
- **Files:** `.github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml`, `ota/sdk/scripts/build.mjs`, `ota/sdk/package.json`, `ota/sdk/src/version.js`, `ota/sdk/CHANGELOG.md`, `ota/sdk/README.md`, `ota/sdk/release/sdk-publish.draft.yml`, `ota/sdk/release/CHANGES.md`, `tools/ci/sdk-draft-pins.test.mjs` (added by lead decision (34e) of 2026-11-20)
- **Steps:**
  1. `build.mjs` copies the OTA part of `@velexis/api-types` into `dist/types/api-types.d.ts` and rewrites the import specifier, so the published package has no dependencies, not even for types.
  2. `sdk-publish.yml`: manual workflow on a tag `sdk-vX.Y.Z`; build, contract test, size check, `npm publish --provenance`; release notes with the SRI hash of the IIFE.
  3. Human step: create the npm organisation and the publishing credential, npm's trusted publishing (for 1.0.0, while the package does not exist and npm cannot configure a trusted publisher for it, a short-lived granular access token as the secret `NPM_TOKEN` of the GitHub environment `npm`); set version `1.0.0`, write the CHANGELOG, tag and run the workflow.
- **Acceptance:**
  - `npm pack` produces a package whose `dist/types` compile in an empty project without `@velexis/api-types` installed (test in CI).
  - The 1.0.0 release exists with provenance (human step recorded in the PR).
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk build && cd ota/sdk && npm pack --dry-run`
- **Note (2026-11-18, ADR-0029 item 9, decisions D5 and D16 approved by the owner on 2026-11-16; SDK-019):** the 1.0.0 package states and declares the Node.js versions the SDK supports, Node.js 22.12 and later and 24: its README (§1 "Runs in", §2, §7 and §8) and `package.json`'s `"engines": { "node": ">=22.12" }`, which `npm pack` carries. CI's non-required job `sdk-node22` runs the SDK's unit and contract tests on 22.12.0 until Node 22's end of life on 2027-04-30; a release after that date states Node.js 24 and later.
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decision (30h), approved by the owner on 2026-11-19; FIX-W61-SDK):** the publishing credential is npm's trusted publishing (OIDC: the publish job's `id-token: write`, no long-lived token). npm configures a trusted publisher only for a package that already exists (npm 11.19.1's own documentation of `npm trust`: "Package must exist"), so 1.0.0 is published with a short-lived granular access token, the secret `NPM_TOKEN` of the GitHub environment `npm`, and every later release with trusted publishing. npm removed its legacy tokens, automation tokens included, in November 2025, so step 3 names none. The draft `sdk-publish.yml`, revised in wave 61 and still only in the scratchpad for the owner's line-by-line approval, takes the credential from its input `credential` (`trusted-publishing` by default, `npm-token` for 1.0.0), never from the secret's presence: npm 11.19.1 publishes with whatever token it is given whenever the trusted publisher's token exchange fails, logging it only at the verbose level (`lib/utils/oidc.js`, `lib/commands/publish.js`), so a trusted-publishing run holds no token and stops with `ENEEDAUTH` instead, and its dry run checks that npm got the trusted publisher's token. The draft's readiness check also refuses a `repository.url` other than that of the repository the run belongs to. The 1.0.0 release commit adds `package.json`'s `repository` field (`"type": "git"`, `"url": "git+https://github.com/bhagwati-prasad/velexis-ota.git"`, `"directory": "ota/sdk"`), which provenance needs; this wave does not add it. The package is kept as built: the packed `package.json` keeps its devDependencies and scripts, `src/` and the source maps ship, and `pack.test.js` uses the system `tar`; its commented 400 s `beforeAll` budget is a new hook's own explicit budget and needs no AGENTS.md §7 approval. Not decided, the owner's: the licence (H-14) and the approval of `sdk-publish.yml`'s lines; `"private": true` and `"license": "UNLICENSED"` stay until then. Sources, read on 2026-11-19: docs.npmjs.com's trusted-publishers, generating-provenance-statements and about-access-tokens pages, from their sources in github.com/npm/documentation because this session's network refuses docs.npmjs.com, and the npm CLI that Node 24 ships. Those pages also say that publishing new versions directly with a granular access token ends in January 2027: a 1.0.0 published after that cannot use the fallback as drafted, which needs the owner's decision, and both calendars of `docs/mvp/plans/roadmap.md` place the publish after it (M6 runs from 10 May to 11 June 2027 with agents, from 3 April to 21 July 2028 without).
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decisions (31f) to (31h), approved by the owner on 2026-11-19; FIX-W62-SDK):** (31f) 1.0.0 is published before January 2027, when npm removes direct publishing with granular access tokens: the owner's licence choice (H-14), the npm organisation, the approval of the draft `sdk-publish.yml`'s lines, the release commit on `main` and the publish happen in December 2026, ahead of the launch block. ### SDK-016 · Share one refresh between the clients derived from one cookie-mode client ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-sdk
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** SDK-004
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js (cookie mode's refresh single flight: `refreshing`, `generation`, `fetchingCsrf`, all per session today) and client.js (`derive`, what `withOptions` starts from); ota/sdk/src/index.js (`withOptions`, which builds a new client with a new session); docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/index.d.ts and shared.d.ts (`withOptions`; never edited, ADR-0019); ota/docs/adr/0006-storefront-cookie-sessions-and-csrf.md (the refresh cookie, its rotation, reuse revoking the family) and 0016-sdk-packaging-and-type-contract.md; ota/frontend/src/pages/booking.js (`rulesClientOf`) and src/boot.js (`clientFor`: the currency client); ota/sdk/README.md (cookie mode: Refresh)
- **Files:** `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`, `ota/sdk/src/internal/client.js`, `ota/sdk/src/index.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-cookie.test.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/options.test.js`, `ota/sdk/README.md`, `ota/sdk/CHANGELOG.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W49-SHARED (lead decision (17d) of 2026-11-11, approved by the owner): every client has its own session, so the clients a page derives with `withOptions` (the storefront's fare-rules client with `maxRetries: 0`, `rulesClientOf`, and its currency client, `clientFor`) each run their own refresh: two of them answered `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` at the same time send `POST /v1/auth/refresh` twice with the same `__Host-vx_rt` cookie, and the API answers the second with `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` and revokes the session's family (OADR-0006). In cookie mode, a client derived with `withOptions` shares its parent's refresh state (the refresh in flight, the count of finished refreshes and the CSRF re-fetch in flight), so one family of derived clients sends one refresh at a time and a call whose attempt went out before a refresh that has finished since is sent again without another; every other option (`maxRetries`, `currency`, `timeoutMs`, headers) stays the derived client's own.
  2. Internal behaviour only: no option, method or type changes, the frozen `docs/velexis-sdk` types and `extensions.md` stay as they are, the contract and parity tests pass unchanged, and the bundle stays within its size budget. Token and server mode keep a session per client, as decision (17d) names cookie mode; the task checks whether two derived token-mode clients with the same `refreshToken` string can present it twice and, if so, writes it down in the PR's questions for a task of its own.
  3. Tests (`session-cookie.test.js`, the fake `fetch`): two clients derived from one cookie-mode client, and a client and its derived one, whose calls are answered `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` at once send exactly one refresh and then each call once more; a refresh refused with `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` rejects every waiting call with that `AuthenticationError` and calls `onSessionExpired` once for that refresh (the README says whose hook when derived clients set different ones); a derived client's `maxRetries: 0` still applies to its own calls only; a CSRF re-fetch is shared the same way. The README's cookie-mode refresh paragraph (§4.1) and the CHANGELOG say so, and the two places that say a derived client "shares nothing mutable" with its parent (the README's §5.1 and the `withOptions` JSDoc of `src/index.js`, which is not a type of the frozen contract) name the refresh state it now shares in cookie mode.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Clients derived with `withOptions` from one cookie-mode client send one `POST /v1/auth/refresh` for any number of their calls answered `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` together, so the storefront's fare-rules and currency clients never present one refresh cookie twice.
  - No public option, method or type changes: the frozen types, the contract test and the parity test pass unchanged.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk typecheck && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk build`

### OAD-023 · Keep the last action's message on the booking page after it re-renders
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-admin
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OAD-022
- **Size:** S
- **Read first:** ota/admin/src/components/confirm-dialog.tsx (the success message beside the trigger, kept in the dialog's own `useActionState`); ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/page.tsx (`bookingActions`: which dialogs a render offers), issue-dialog.tsx, cancel-dialog.tsx and review-dialog.tsx; actions.ts (`withWarnings`, `revalidateBooking`, the success strings of `issueTickets`, `cancelBooking` and `closeBookingReview`); sections.tsx (`BookingDetail` and its action bar); ota/admin/docs/routes.md (the booking page); ota/admin/README.md §9 (the confirmation dialogs); docs/mvp/conventions.md §3 (Next.js apps: the server actions' state, labels and `aria-describedby`); tools/e2e/README.md (the OTA admin's helpers)
- **Files:** `ota/admin/src/components/confirm-dialog.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/components/confirm-dialog.test.tsx`, `ota/admin/README.md`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/action-outcome.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/issue-dialog.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/cancel-dialog.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/review-dialog.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/sections.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/page.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/dialogs.test.tsx`, `ota/admin/src/app/(console)/bookings/[bookingId]/page.test.tsx`, `ota/admin/docs/routes.md`, `tools/e2e/specs/ota-admin/reconciliation-review.e2e.ts`, `tools/e2e/specs/ota-admin/sso-bookings.e2e.ts`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W51-OTA (lead decision (20l) of 2026-11-13, approved by the owner, after OAD-022): `ConfirmDialog` shows an action's success message beside its trigger, from the dialog's own `useActionState`. After **Issue tickets**, **Cancel the booking** and **Close the review** the action revalidates the booking's page, and the new render usually no longer offers the action (`canIssue`, `canCancel` or `closeReviewOffered` is false for a booking ticketed, cancelled, waiting for the airline's answer to a cancellation request or out of the review), so the dialog unmounts with its state: the message ("Tickets issued.", "Booking cancelled.", "Cancellation requested from the airline: the booking is not cancelled yet.", "Review closed: …") and the warnings of the action's answer that `withWarnings` appends to it (an order Amadeus no longer had, the request to the airline and what to do next) disappear as the page shows the new status, before staff or a screen reader can take them in. The page's next `console.bookings.get` (without `refresh`) does not repeat those warnings, so nothing else on the page shows them.
  2. Keep the last outcome on the page instead: a client component of the booking page (`action-outcome.tsx`) above the action bar in `BookingDetail`, at a place and key that the revalidation keeps (keyed by the booking's id, so another booking starts empty), holds the last success of these three dialogs and shows it in one polite `role="status"` region, the warnings as their own lines. `ConfirmDialog` gains an optional way to hand its success state up (an `onSuccess` callback or a context the three dialogs read); a dialog that hands it up shows no second copy beside its trigger, and every other dialog (capture, refund, resync, the note, the edits, the settings deletes) keeps the message beside its trigger as today. The region keeps the message until the next action on the page succeeds or fails, or another booking opens; a reload clears it (nothing is stored, in the browser or the URL, and no personal data is added to the message). A refusal stays in the dialog, without a change, as today.
  3. Tests: `confirm-dialog.test.tsx` (the success state handed up once per success, and the message beside the trigger when nothing takes it); `dialogs.test.tsx` (each of the three dialogs hands up its message with the API's warnings); `page.test.tsx` (a re-render of the booking without the action keeps the message in the status region, another booking's page starts without it); `reconciliation-review.e2e.ts` (after each closure the message is on the page once the status badge shows `Failed` or `Confirmed` and "Close the review" is gone) and `sso-bookings.e2e.ts` (the same after Issue and Cancel), axe on each page with the message. Update the booking page in `routes.md` and the confirmation dialogs in the README's §9.
- **Acceptance:**
  - After Issue tickets, Cancel the booking or Close the review succeeds, the booking page shows the action's success message and the API's warnings in a status region once it has re-rendered with the new status, although the action's button is gone; the message stays until the next action on the page or another booking opens, and nothing of it is stored.
  - A refusal still shows in its dialog without a change; the other dialogs keep their message beside their trigger; axe reports no serious or critical violation on the page with the message.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin test && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-admin build && E2E_WITH_OTA=1 pnpm test:e2e -- --project=ota-admin specs/ota-admin/reconciliation-review.e2e.ts specs/ota-admin/sso-bookings.e2e.ts`
- **Note (2026-11-13, lead decision (20l), approved by the owner, FIX-W51-OTA):** OAD-023 runs after the launch and keeps its M6 tag: a named exception to the M6 go criterion "every task done", as PBE-064, X-042 and X-043 are ([roadmap](../../../docs/mvp/plans/roadmap.md) §2.0 and the M6 go/no-go, [ADR-0025](../../../docs/mvp/adr/0025-roadmap-scheduling-and-tracking.md) item 4). Until it is merged the page already shows the new status and the timeline's event; the action loses its one-line message and the warnings of its answer (for a cancellation that went to the airline as a request, the overview still says "Cancellation requested, not completed", without what to do next). The roadmap's re-baseline of 2026-11-13 (FIX-W51-SHARED) places it after the launch in both calendars. This Note changes no Status.

### SDK-017 · Share one refresh per refresh token in token and server mode, and send a shared cookie-mode refresh with the root client's settings ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-sdk
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** SDK-016
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/sdk/README.md §4.1 (SDK-016's shared cookie-mode refresh and whose settings it uses), §4.2 ("Derived clients keep a session each": what SDK-016 found) and §4.3 (rotating refresh tokens and concurrency), and the CHANGELOG; ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js and client.js, and ota/sdk/src/index.js (`withOptions`, `derive`); ota/sdk/test/unit/session-token.test.js, session-server.test.js, session-cookie.test.js and options.test.js; docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/index.d.ts and shared.d.ts (never edited, ADR-0019); the OTA backend's refresh endpoint (reuse detection: a refresh token presented twice answers `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` and revokes the family); ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md §4 (one client per visitor on a server)
- **Files:** `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`, `ota/sdk/src/internal/client.js`, `ota/sdk/src/index.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-token.test.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-server.test.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-cookie.test.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/options.test.js`, `ota/sdk/README.md`, `ota/sdk/CHANGELOG.md`, `ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by the lead for wave 51 (decision (20f) of 2026-11-13, approved by the owner; found by SDK-016): in token and server mode a client and any client derived from it with `withOptions` hold the same refresh token unless one sets another, so at the next `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` both present it and the API answers the second `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` and revokes the whole session. Share the refresh between clients of one family that present the same refresh token: one refresh in flight per refresh-token value, whose result (the new tokens) every client that presented that value takes, reported once through `onSessionRefreshed`. Clients holding different refresh tokens (a server's per-visitor clients) never share anything; a token function's value is read per call as today. A refresh token that has been rotated is never presented again by any client of the family.
  2. Cookie mode: the shared refresh and the shared CSRF fetch go out with the transport settings of the family's root client (the one `createVelexisClient` made: `maxRetries`, `timeoutMs`, `headers`, `fetch`, `onResponse`), not with those of the client whose call came first, so the outcome no longer depends on which `401` arrived first; the `onSessionExpired` of the client whose call started the refresh is called once, as SDK-016 built.
  3. Tests (fake `fetch`): in token mode and in server mode, a client and its derived client (derived before and after a refresh), and two clients derived with the same `refreshToken` string, answered `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` at once and one after the other, send one refresh per token and never `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`; two clients with different refresh tokens refresh separately and never take each other's tokens; in cookie mode a refresh started by a `maxRetries: 0` client and answered `503` is retried with the root's settings, and every waiting call succeeds.
  4. README §4.1, §4.2 and §4.3 and the CHANGELOG say what is shared and when; §4.2's advice to derive per-user clients from a client without a refresh token is replaced or kept as the tests show; the build-your-own-frontend guide §4 follows.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Token and server mode: clients of one family that hold the same refresh token send one refresh per token value and never get `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` from each other; clients with different refresh tokens share nothing.
  - Cookie mode: a shared refresh or CSRF fetch uses the root client's transport settings whichever client started it.
  - The storefront (booking.js, boot.js) works unchanged, and the frozen contract files are untouched.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test && E2E_WITH_OTA=1 pnpm test:e2e --project=storefront`
- **Note (2026-11-13, lead decision (21c), approved by the owner, FIX-W52-SDK):** SDK-017 is accepted as built. In token and server mode only the hooks of the client whose call started a shared refresh run, once: its `onSessionRefreshed` (and `onStaffSessionRefreshed`) with the new tokens, or for a refresh refused with `401` its `onSessionExpired`, while every call waiting for that refresh gets the same result or `AuthenticationError`; a derived client keeps its parent's hooks unless it sets its own. In cookie mode the family's shared refresh and CSRF fetch go out with the whole transport of the family's root client (`baseUrl`, `maxRetries`, `timeoutMs`, `headers`, `fetch`, `onResponse`, `locale`, `currency`, `host` and `endUser`; only the starting call's `host`, `endUser` and `X-Velexis-*` headers go with them), whichever client's call started them. This Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-13, lead decisions (21d) and (21e), approved by the owner, FIX-W52-SDK):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0. (21d) A refresh token the family has rotated leads to the family's newest tokens (`resolveRefresh` of `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`, which replaces `follow` and the family lookup of `refreshTokens`) only (1) for a client that held that value as its own string `refreshToken` before the family recorded the rotation (configured when the client was made or derived, or taken from a refresh or session result it took part in, or from an earlier rotation it followed; the family's rotations carry their order, `seq`, and the client the count at which it began to hold its token, `heldSince`), at any later time and along any chain of rotations, or (2) within 10 s of the rotation (`ROTATION_WINDOW_MS`, beside `FAMILY_TOKENS_KEPT`, the window of the build-your-own-frontend guide's §8.2; inclusive, measured with `Date.now()`, a clock set back counting as outside). Any other client that presents a rotated refresh token later (a server's per-request client made from the root with a visitor's rotated refresh token, a token function that still gives it, in token and in server mode) sends it to the API as it is: the reuse detection answers `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` and revokes the session, and the SDK reports it as any refused refresh (the starting client's `onSessionExpired`, the `AuthenticationError` to waiting calls). SDK-016's and SDK-017's guarantees hold: a client derived before a refresh never presents the rotated token at any later time, clients with different tokens share nothing, one refresh per token value is in flight, and a refresh leaves `Family.refreshing` as soon as the family has recorded its rotation, so a call after the window never joins it while the starting client's hooks run. (21e) A client's own record of replaced access tokens (SDK-008; `latest` for a string `accessToken`) gives a newer access token for an old one only together with the refresh token of the same session (`resolveAccess`): when the call's refresh-token source or string gives that session's newest refresh token, or a value that leads to it under (21d); an expired access token presented with no refresh token, another session's or an unknown one is sent as it is (`401 TOKEN_EXPIRED`), so a refresh-token function is also read before a request whose access token the client replaced, and a client without a refresh token keeps its configured access token after a session result. Proven by `session-token.test.js` and `session-server.test.js` (`[FIX-W52-SDK AC1]`, `[FIX-W52-SDK AC2]`, fake timers and a fake API whose reuse detection revokes the session: the per-request client 9 s and 11 s after the rotation, the client of the refresh and a client derived before it with token functions, the AsyncLocalStorage clients, the holder at 11 s, an hour and along a chain, the 10 000 ms boundary, a clock set back, a refresh whose hook still runs, a token function that took the tokens 9 s after the rotation, a sign-in's replaced tokens, a password change by a client that presents a rotated refresh token as it is (the family records the rotation of the session's newest refresh token, and the rotated token's window never opens again), an old access token whose session another client rotated again; 21 of the 33 fail on the code before the fix, and the 12 others prove the guarantees it keeps) and mutation checks of the time, holder, access-token and flight conditions; README §4.2, §4.3 and §5.1, `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md` §2, the CHANGELOG and the guide's §4 and §8.2 state the rules. This Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-15, lead decisions (22g) to (22j), approved by the owner, FIX-W53-SDK):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0. (22g) A client given a string `accessToken` and no `refreshToken` (neither a string nor a function) is exempt from (21e): after its own `auth.signIn`, `auth.refresh` or `auth.changePassword` it sends the result's access token again, as under SDK-008, and `withOptions` starts from it (`accessOnly` in `resolveAccess` of `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`, where (21e) returns the value when the call presents no refresh token); it never refreshes, no other client's result reaches it, and every other client keeps (21e). (22h) In the rotation window a negative age (the clock set back) counts as inside while it is no more than `ROTATION_WINDOW_MS` and outside beyond that (`withinWindow`), so a normal clock correction never revokes a visitor's session and the window never spans more than 20 s. (22i) A call that starts or joins a shared refresh is marked as a holder of the new refresh token as of the moment it joined (`refreshTokens` passes the family's count of rotations at that moment to `take`), not after the starting client's hooks have run, so a rotation of the brand-new token by another holder while those hooks run is followed at any later time (wave 52's N14 case). (22j) Two behaviours beyond (21d) and (21e)'s wording are accepted as built: a refresh leaves `Family.refreshing` as soon as the family has recorded its rotation, and for a token function the family's record of a rotated value is checked before the client's own. Proven by `session-token.test.js` (`[FIX-W53-SDK AC1]` to `[FIX-W53-SDK AC3]`, in token and server mode, fake timers and `vi.setSystemTime`, no wall clock: the access-only client after each of the three calls, with no `refreshToken` and with `refreshToken: null`, two clients of the family that hold the old access token alone and never get its result (one derived from the root, one derived from the signing-in client before its sign-in), and four clients that keep (21e); a clock set back 5 s and 15 s for the three late clients and for token functions after a sign-in, and the 10 000 ms bound; the N14 case with a 20 s hook, for the starting and the waiting client): 22 of the 38 new tests fail on the code before the fix, the others prove the rules it keeps; mutation checks of the exemption's condition, the bound (dropped, exclusive, doubled, 1 ms narrower or wider, no lower bound) and the holder mark (reverted, for the starter only, for the waiter only) fail tests. The literal N14 mutation (`take` never updates `heldSince`) now behaves like the fix wherever a test can reach, so no test tells them apart: the family can record a rotation of a refresh token a client takes only after the client took it, except during `adopt`'s wait for a slow access-token function of a client with a string `refreshToken`, where another holder that followed the result's rotation would have to rotate the result's refresh token (after the brand-new access token expired); `adopt` marks the client when it takes the result, and the mutant would follow that rotation. README §4.2 and §4.3, `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md` §2, the CHANGELOG and the guide's §4 and §8.2 state the rules. This Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-15, lead decisions (23f) to (23h), approved by the owner, FIX-W54-SDK):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0. (23f) Wave 52's mutation N14 (`take` never updates `heldSince`) is accepted as an equivalent mutant: no test has to kill it, and `take` keeps its `heldSince` update. With (23g) it is equivalent in `adopt`'s case too: the whole SDK suite (1045 tests) passes with it. (23g) A client adopting its own session result (`auth.signIn`, `auth.refresh`, `auth.changePassword`) is marked as a holder of the result's refresh token as of the moment the result arrived: `adopt` of `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js` takes the family's count of rotations before it awaits `heldTokens` or a token function and passes it to `take`. And `adopt` never replaces newer tokens the client already follows: when `heldTokens` has followed the family's rotation of the result's refresh token past it (`resolveRefresh` took the newer tokens), `latest` keeps those newer tokens, and the values the client held lead to them in its own record; `onSessionRefreshed` still gets the result's session. (23h) An access token that is an empty string counts as no access token everywhere: `accessOnly` requires a non-empty string, and `options()` (so `withOptions`) and `holdsTokens` treat `""` as `tokenOf` does (one `accessString`), so a client configured with `accessToken: ""` behaves exactly as one configured with none. Proven by `session-token.test.js` (`[FIX-W54-SDK AC1]` and `[FIX-W54-SDK AC2]`, in token and server mode, fake timers, no wall clock): a client with a slow access-token function and a string refresh token whose `auth.refresh` result's refresh token another holder rotates during `adopt`'s await follows that rotation after the window (before the fix `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` from the fake API), also when it already follows newer tokens of another session (it takes the result's session, not those); a client whose `adopt` followed past the result keeps the newer tokens, sends the newest access token for the one its function still gives without a refresh, and presents the newest refresh token even after 512 refreshes of another session have pushed the result's out of the family (before the fix `REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`); and a client with `accessToken: ""` and no `refreshToken`, `refreshToken: null` or a string refresh token makes the same requests with the same outcomes as the same client without `accessToken`, before and after its own sign-in, on its next call, through `withOptions` and in what the family learns from its `auth.refresh`. All 12 new tests fail on the code before the fix. Mutation checks fail tests: the mark taken after the awaits (4), `latest` overwritten by the result (2), the newer tokens kept without checking that they are the result's session's (2), kept without the own record that leads the values the client held to them (2), `options()` reading `""` (2), `holdsTokens` counting `""` (4), `accessString` accepting `""` (6); `accessOnly` alone accepting `""` survives as an equivalent mutant, since every value it is compared with is non-empty (`tokenOf`, `accessString`). README §4.2 and §4.3, `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md` §2, the CHANGELOG (ESM 16 095 B min+gzip, 47 B more), `client.js`'s JSDoc and the build-your-own-frontend guide §4 and §8.2 state the rules. This Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-15, lead decisions (24l) to (24n), approved by the owner, SDK-018):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0; SDK-018 carries them out. (24l) When `adopt` of `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js` keeps newer tokens the client already follows ((23g) above), `onSessionRefreshed` gets the result's session with those newer tokens: `accessToken` and `refreshToken` are the newer pair, every other field (`accessTokenExpiresAt`, `refreshTokenExpiresAt`, `tokenType`, `subject`) is the result's; in every other case it still gets `result.session` itself, so (23g)'s "`onSessionRefreshed` still gets the result's session" holds for that case only. A store that every client's hook writes (the build-your-own-frontend guide's §8.2 pattern) then ends with the newest pair instead of the rotated one, and the visitor's next request after the window succeeds instead of `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`; the errata candidate for identity.d.ts and shared.d.ts is in `ota/backend/openapi/README.md` §7. (24m) A refresh token that is an empty string counts as no refresh token everywhere, as (23h) made `""` no access token: one non-empty `refreshString` (and `refreshSource`) feeds `accessOnly`, `refreshes()`, `resolveRefresh`, `sessionAccessToken`, `holdsTokens` and `options()`. (24n) Cookie mode keeps refusing every token option that is set, `""` included. Proven by SDK-018's tests (`[SDK-018 AC1]` to `[SDK-018 AC3]`); this Note changes no Status.
