### SDK-018 · Give onSessionRefreshed the newer tokens a client keeps over its own session result, and treat an empty refresh token as none ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-sdk
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** SDK-017
- **Size:** S
- **Read first:** ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js (`adopt`, `heldTokens`, `take`, `latest`, `accessString`, `accessOnly`, `holdsTokens`, `tokenOf`, `refreshes`, `resolveRefresh`, `resolveAccess`, `options`, the `onSessionRefreshed` calls) and client.js; ota/sdk/test/unit/session-token.test.js (FIX-W53-SDK's and FIX-W54-SDK's blocks: `rotatingApi`, `slowSource`, `rotatedWhileAdopting`, `sessionCallsWith`, fake timers), session-server.test.js, session-cookie.test.js, namespaces-auth.test.js and options.test.js; ota/sdk/README.md §4.2 and §4.3, the CHANGELOG and docs/extensions.md §2; ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md §4 and §8.2 (a store that `onSessionRefreshed` writes); docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/identity.d.ts and shared.d.ts (`onSessionRefreshed`; never edited, ADR-0019); ota/backend/openapi/README.md §7 (errata candidates); SDK-017's block and its dated notes (FIX-W52-SDK to FIX-W54-SDK)
- **Files:** `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`, `ota/sdk/src/internal/client.js`, `ota/sdk/src/shared.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-token.test.js`, `ota/sdk/test/unit/session-cookie.test.js`, `ota/sdk/README.md`, `ota/sdk/CHANGELOG.md`, `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md`, `ota/frontend/docs/build-your-own-frontend.md`, `ota/backend/openapi/README.md`, `ota/docs/plans/agent-tasks.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by the lead for wave 55 (decisions (24l) to (24n) of 2026-11-15, approved by the owner; FIX-W54-SDK's review raised them), before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0. (24l) When `adopt` keeps newer tokens the client already follows (lead decision (23g): reading the client's token sources followed the family's rotation of the result's refresh token past it), `onSessionRefreshed` gets the result's session with those newer tokens: `accessToken` and `refreshToken` are the newer pair, and every other field (`accessTokenExpiresAt`, `refreshTokenExpiresAt`, `tokenType`, `subject`) is the result's, the same customer and session. `refreshTokenExpiresAt` is the session's absolute end, the same for every pair of a session; `accessTokenExpiresAt` is the result's access token's, which the newer one's never precedes, so a store that times its cookies by it lets the access cookie lapse early, never late. In every other case the hook gets `result.session` itself, as before. The result the call resolves with is unchanged. Record an errata candidate (dated 2026-11-15, (24l)) in ota/backend/openapi/README.md §7, where the contract's errata candidates are kept: identity.d.ts's `auth.refresh` description ("the SDK's automatic refresh passes `result.session` to `onSessionRefreshed`") should mention this case; docs/velexis-sdk stays unedited.
  2. (24m) A refresh token that is an empty string counts as no refresh token everywhere, as `accessString` does for the access token (lead decision (23h)): one non-empty `refreshString` (and `refreshSource`, a non-empty string or a function) feeds `accessOnly`, `refreshes()`, `resolveRefresh`, `sessionAccessToken`, `holdsTokens` and `options()`, so a client made with `refreshToken: ""` behaves exactly as one made without `refreshToken` or with `null`. (24n) Cookie mode keeps refusing every token option that is set, `accessToken: ""`, `refreshToken: ""` and `bookingToken: ""` included, at construction and in `withOptions`.
  3. Tests (`session-token.test.js` in token and in server mode, fake timers and the strict fake API of FIX-W52-SDK, no wall clock; `session-cookie.test.js`): a store that every client's `onSessionRefreshed` writes (the guide's §8.2 pattern) ends with the newer pair, and the visitor's next request after the window succeeds instead of `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`; the hook gets exactly the fields above; a plain `auth.refresh`, `auth.signIn` and `auth.changePassword`, and a client that follows newer tokens of another session, still give the hook `result.session` itself; `refreshToken: ""` with no access token, a string one or a function makes the same requests with the same outcomes as no `refreshToken`, before and after its own sign-in, on its next call, through `withOptions` and in what the family learns; a call refused `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED` is neither refreshed nor sent again; cookie mode refuses the three empty token options. Mutation-check every changed line.
  4. Docs: README §4.2 and §4.3, the CHANGELOG (bundle size from `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk build`), docs/extensions.md §2, the JSDoc of client.js, session.js and shared.js (`refreshToken`: `""` is none), the build-your-own-frontend guide §4 and §8.2, and a dated note in SDK-017's block.
- **Acceptance:**
  - In token and server mode, when `adopt` keeps newer tokens the client already follows, `onSessionRefreshed` gets the result's session with the newer `accessToken` and `refreshToken` and the result's other fields, so a store written by every client's hook ends with the newest pair and the visitor's next request after the 10 s window succeeds; in every other case it gets `result.session` itself.
  - A client made with `refreshToken: ""` behaves exactly as one made without `refreshToken`: no refresh, no resend, the same session results, `withOptions` and family records.
  - Cookie mode refuses `accessToken: ""`, `refreshToken: ""` and `bookingToken: ""` at construction and in `withOptions`.
  - No option, method or type changes, docs/velexis-sdk is untouched and the errata candidate is recorded; the storefront's booking.js and boot.js work unchanged.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk typecheck && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk build && E2E_WITH_OTA=1 pnpm test:e2e --project=storefront`
- **Note (2026-11-16, lead decisions (25k) to (25m), approved by the owner with "yes to all", FIX-W56-SDK):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0; a fix under SDK-018, which stays done. (25k) `onSessionRefreshed` gets the family's newest tokens of the result's session whenever the family has rotated the result's refresh token by the time the hook is called, for every kind of client, not only when `adopt` keeps newer tokens the client already follows ((24l) above): a refresh-token function that reads the integrator's store, a string refresh token the client did not hold, a client that follows another session's tokens, after an explicit `auth.refresh` or an `auth.changePassword` (SDK-018's questions and its review's probe). The client keeps those newest tokens too (`adopt` takes them instead of the result's, so every value it held leads to them; holding the result's refresh token since it arrived, (23g), now works through that read, and `adopt` no longer needs the count of rotations at arrival), so a client whose token functions already give the newest pair never leads it back to the result's rotated one. SDK-018's test "the hook gets result.session itself when a client that follows newer tokens of another session takes its result, also when another holder rotated the result's refresh token while adopt waited" pinned the old behaviour; it now asserts the (25k) rule (`[FIX-W56-SDK AC1]`). (25l) Every other field of the reported session (`accessTokenExpiresAt`, `refreshTokenExpiresAt`, `tokenType`, `subject`) stays the result's, early, never late, as README §4.2 and the build-your-own-frontend guide §8.2 say. (25m) The errata candidate in `ota/backend/openapi/README.md` §7 is extended for (25k) and records that shared.d.ts's "when set" wording for `refreshToken` does not hold for `""` since (24m). Proven by FIX-W56-SDK's tests (`[FIX-W56-SDK AC1]`, `[FIX-W56-SDK AC2]` in `session-token.test.js`, token and server mode); this Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-16, lead decision (26j), approved by the owner with "yes to all", FIX-W57-SDK):** before SDK-015 publishes 1.0.0; a fix under SDK-018, which stays done. `onStaffSessionRefreshed` (the automatic refresh of a `sessionKind: "staff"` client) gets the family's newest tokens of the staff session whenever the staff refresh token it would report has been rotated by the time it is called, as (25k) does for `onSessionRefreshed`: the automatic refresh calls it once the starting client's `onSessionRefreshed` has finished, and another client of the family that holds the brand-new refresh token may have rotated it meanwhile (the (22i) case, FIX-W56-SDK's question 19). `runRefresh` reads the family's record right before the staff hook, with no await in between, and gives it the whole `ConsoleStaffSession` with the newest `accessToken` and `refreshToken` in `session` and every other field the result's (the session's expiries, type and subject, and `staff`, `tenant`, `permissions` and `environments` of that refresh); otherwise it gets the result itself, and `onSessionRefreshed` is unchanged. Before, the staff hook reported the result's already-rotated pair, so staff cookies it wrote after the other client's hook ended with the rotated refresh token, which the staff member's next request after the 10 s window presented (`401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`, a revoked session). The OTA admin's staff clients (an access token only, refreshes through its own de-duplicated `console.auth.refresh`) are unaffected: neither hook runs for them. Internal behaviour only: no option, method or type changed, docs/velexis-sdk is untouched. README §4.2 and §4.3, the CHANGELOG, docs/extensions.md §2, the JSDoc of session.js, client.js and namespaces/console.js, and the errata candidate in `ota/backend/openapi/README.md` §7 (extended for `onStaffSessionRefreshed`, dated 2026-11-16) say so; the build-your-own-frontend guide shows no staff hook. Proven by FIX-W57-SDK's tests (`[FIX-W57-SDK AC1]` to `[FIX-W57-SDK AC3]` in `session-server.test.js`, token and server mode); this Note changes no Status.

### OBE-103 · Measure the OTA API and worker on Node.js 24 against Node 22 and the VM budget ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** X-048, OBE-088
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/adr/0029-nodejs-24-runtime.md (items 3 and 5); ota/docs/performance.md §1, §4 (Step 4), §5, §6 and §9; ota/backend/test/load/README.md; docs/mvp/runbooks/node-upgrade.md §2; docs/mvp/architecture.md §3 (memory budget); docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md §14; the blocks of OBE-088, OBE-096 and X-050
- **Files:** `ota/docs/performance.md`, `ota/backend/test/load/README.md`, `ota/backend/test/load/search-load.mjs` (its measuring preload PRELOAD_SOURCE and its report), `ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs` (its report), `ota/docs/plans/agent-tasks.md` (its status)
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by the lead for the Node.js 24 upgrade (ADR-0029 items 3 and 5). One commit, one build, one set of flags (the units' `NODE_OPTIONS`, which the scripts read from the unit files since X-050), two runtimes: Node 22.23.x (`/opt/node22/bin` on the agents' machine) and Node 24.22.x or newer (the `.nvmrc` major), each first on `PATH` for the whole run, `node --version` recorded. Run under the machine's e2e lock with a scratch database and a Redis of its own, as §6 did, with `nproc` and the load average beside every figure. The older records of §4 and §6 used other flags (16 MiB semi-spaces outside a memory limit), so both runtimes are measured here rather than compared with them.
  2. Add the time spent in garbage collection to the measuring preload (`PRELOAD_SOURCE` in search-load.mjs: a `PerformanceObserver` on `gc` entries, summed per minute) and to both scripts' reports, if they lack it. Then search-load.mjs at OBE-096's settings (10 visitors, the default offers per search), three runs per runtime, and booking-load.mjs `--tenants 5 --minutes 30`, one run per runtime. Record p50 and p95 per operation, the peak RSS of the API and the worker against 768 and 512 MiB, PostgreSQL connections, Redis memory, the queue latency per queue, and the share of time in garbage collection of the API and of the worker.
  3. Write a new section at the end, "§10 Node.js 24 (OBE-103, <date>)", with both runtimes side by side. §2 to §9 stay as written; add one dated note under §4 Step 4 (the 16 MiB it calls V8's default was the default outside a memory limit; under the unit's `MemoryMax` Node picks its own value, and since X-050 every unit pins one) and one under §6 (that run's worker had 16 MiB semi-spaces; the VM's has 1 MiB). Add any follow-up to §9. Update ota/backend/test/load/README.md where it describes the figures.
  4. If Node 24 is more than 10 % worse at any p95, leaves less than 64 MiB between a peak RSS and its `MemoryMax`, or the API or the worker spends more than 5 % of its time in garbage collection with its pinned semi-space, stop and report the figures: a change of a unit's flags is a lead decision and a task of its own.
- **Acceptance:**
  - §10 holds both runtimes' figures from the same build and the units' flags: three search runs and one 30-minute booking run each, with the garbage-collection share.
  - On Node 24 every p95 is within 10 % of Node 22's, the API's and the worker's peak RSS stay at least 64 MiB under 768 and 512 MiB, and neither spends more than 5 % of its time in garbage collection; or the pull request names the regression and the follow-up the lead must decide.
  - The earlier sections are unchanged apart from the two dated notes and §9's follow-ups.
- **Verify:** `node --check ota/backend/test/load/search-load.mjs && node --check ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs && node ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs --tenants 5 --minutes 30`
- **Note (2026-11-18, lead decisions (29b) and (29d) of 2026-11-18, approved by the owner with "yes to all"; FIX-W60-SHARED):** "5 % of its time in garbage collection" (step 4 and the acceptance) means the main-thread garbage-collection pause time over the process's elapsed (wall-clock) time, which the measuring preload sums ([`ota/docs/performance.md`](../performance.md) §10). The share of CPU time is recorded for information and is no bound: the worker's pauses are 9.2 % of its CPU time on Node 22 and 8.8 % on Node 24 with its pinned 1 MiB semi-space, while it is idle most of the time, and one API search run (S24-2) reached 5.8 %; no unit flag changes. The runs are accepted as recorded: B24, which started at a 1-minute load average of 5.80 (under the repeat rule's 6) after another agent's locked run; the report-only change of `booking-load.mjs` between B22 and B24 (no garbage-collection share for a last timeline window under 30 s); and the two small single-process checks another agent ran beside B24 (a typecheck of `ota/backend` and an ESLint run on one file, about 02:47 and 02:48 UTC, while B24's 1-minute load average stayed below 1.0). This Note changes no Status.

Add `sdk-node22` to node-major.test.mjs's exemption list. ci-workflow.test.mjs asserts that the job runs Node 22.12.0, restores no Turborepo cache and is not one of the six required checks (`[SDK-019 AC2]`); tools/ci/README.md lists it with its end: after Node 22's end of life on 2027-04-30 a task removes it and the docs say Node 24.
  2. The stated range, with the job: Node.js 22.12 and later and 24 (`require()` of the ES module build is on by default from 22.12.0, CHANGELOG_V22 "require(esm) is now enabled by default"; 22.12.x still prints an `ExperimentalWarning` when the requiring file is outside `node_modules`, gone from 22.13.0), evergreen browsers and edge runtimes; without the owner's approval of the job: Node.js 24 and later. Say it the same way in ota/sdk/README.md (the "Runs in" row and §2), types-and-builds.md, build-your-own-frontend.md, tech-stack.md §3's SDK row, dated revisions of ADR-0019 and OADR-0016 pointing at ADR-0029, and `engines.node` in ota/sdk/package.json (`>=22.12` with the job, `>=24` without), which SDK-015 publishes. The comments of the seven code files name "the supported Node versions (README)" instead of Node 22; no logic changes, and bundle.test.js's `require()` probe stays.
  3. CHANGELOG.md, Unreleased: the supported Node versions are stated, declared in `engines` and tested (docs, package metadata and CI only, no API change). A dated note in SDK-015 (publish 1.0.0): its README and `engines` carry this range.
- **Acceptance:**
  - ota/sdk/README.md, types-and-builds.md, the guide, tech-stack.md, the ADR revisions and `engines.node` in ota/sdk/package.json state one range, and it is the range CI runs (`[SDK-019 AC1]`).

### OBE-104 · Run the OTA API and worker for three hours on Node.js 24 and show whether their memory settles ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M6
- **Depends on:** OBE-103
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** ota/docs/performance.md §10 (OBE-103's runs B22 and B24); ota/backend/test/load/README.md; docs/mvp/adr/0029-nodejs-24-runtime.md (items 3 and 5, Results); docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md §14; docs/mvp/runbooks/node-upgrade.md §5 (the VM's MemoryPeak check); the blocks of OBE-088 and OBE-103
- **Files:** `ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs` (its samples and report), `ota/backend/test/load/README.md`, `ota/docs/performance.md` (a new §11 and one §9 line), `ota/docs/plans/agent-tasks.md` (this block and its status)
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by the lead on 2026-11-18 (decision (29c)). In OBE-103's 30-minute run B24 on Node 24, the worker's RSS only ever rose, in steps after each 5-minute scan (about 4 MiB over the last 20 minutes), while its JS heap stayed flat, and the API's RSS rose about 0.23 MiB a minute; on Node 22 the worker gave the memory back within seconds. Thirty minutes cannot tell memory that settles from a slow leak, and the VM's MemoryPeak check takes one reading.
  2. booking-load.mjs: add heapTotal, external and arrayBuffers to each 5-second sample of the API and the worker (the measuring preload already sends rss and heapUsed), and to the report and the JSON: per process, a table per 30 minutes and the least-squares slope of each figure in MiB per minute with r² over minutes 30–90, 90–180 and the last 60. Where the timeline or the garbage-collection figures assume 30 minutes, make them work for 180.
  3. One run on Node 24 (`/opt/node24/bin` first on `PATH` for the API, the worker and the script; `node --version` recorded): `--tenants 5 --minutes 180` with OBE-103's settings otherwise (one build of the merged base made on Node 24, the units' flags, a scratch database, and a Redis of its own set up as the VM's: maxmemory 512mb, noeviction). The run measures memory, not latency, so it holds the machine's soak lock (`/home/user/wt/soak.lock`) rather than the e2e lock, and records `nproc` and the 1-minute load average every 5 minutes.
  4. A process's memory settles if its RSS slope over minutes 90–180 is below 0.02 MiB per minute (about 1 MiB an hour) and its JS heap's slope over the same window is not above that. For a process that does not settle, take two heap snapshots of it 30 minutes apart in a second run of at least 60 minutes (`--heapsnapshot-signal`), compare them by constructor (count and retained size) with a small script kept beside the run outputs, and record the largest growers. Never change a unit's flags: a change is a lead decision and a task of its own.
  5. Write "§11 Three hours on Node.js 24 (OBE-104, <date>)" in ota/docs/performance.md with the 30-minute tables, the slopes, the load and the verdict, and one §9 line for any follow-up. Update ota/backend/test/load/README.md where it describes the samples and the report.
- **Acceptance:**
  - §11 records one 180-minute Node 24 run from one build with the units' flags: RSS, heapUsed, heapTotal, external and arrayBuffers of the API and the worker per 30 minutes, the slopes with r², and the load.
  - The API and the worker both settle by step 4's rule; or §11 names the process that does not, the heap-snapshot comparison and the follow-up the lead must decide.
- **Verify:** `node --check ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs && node ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs --tenants 5 --minutes 180`
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decisions (30a), (30b) and (30c) of 2026-11-19, approved by the owner; FIX-W61-MEMORY):** the memory is accepted as measured, with no new task now (30a): the throwaway VM's checks of `docs/mvp/runbooks/node-upgrade.md` §5 gain step 9, in which the OTA worker and the API beside it run for at least 8 hours, up to 24, under the rehearsal's traffic with their memory sampled every minute (RSS only: a unit's JS heap cannot be read without changing the unit), and a process still rising by the rule after 8 hours becomes a follow-up task then. A later memory re-check judges the JS heap by its floor after the collections (30b): the least-squares slope over minutes 90–180 of the least heap used of each 5 minutes must not be above 0.02 MiB a minute, while RSS keeps step 4's rule; `booking-load.mjs` computes it since FIX-W61-MEMORY (`--floor-minutes`, tested in `tools/perf/booking-load-memory.test.mjs`), and ota/docs/performance.md §11 re-judges R180 with it: neither process settles either, the API on its heap floor (+0.0351 MiB a minute, r² 0.08) and the worker on its RSS (+0.0241). The second acceptance criterion is met by its alternative, so the Status stays done (30c). The offers finding of §11 became OBE-105 (decision (30d)).
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decision (31a), approved by the owner, FIX-W62-DOCS):** the OTA API's verdict by (30b)'s heap-floor rule is recorded as inconclusive by measurement noise: with 5-minute floor windows its floor slope over minutes 90–180 is +0.0351 MiB a minute (r² 0.08, standard error 0.029, larger than the 0.02 bound), and floor windows of 1 to 15 minutes give +0.009 to +0.068, so ninety minutes of its floors cannot resolve the bound. The rule and its 5-minute window stay; the throwaway VM's run of 8 to 24 hours ([`node-upgrade.md`](../../../docs/mvp/runbooks/node-upgrade.md) §5 step 9, judged on RSS) decides ([`performance.md`](../performance.md) §11). This Note changes no Status.

- **Status:** todo

- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/shopping/offers-purge.processor.ts`, `ota/backend/src/shopping/offers-purge.processor.test.ts`, `ota/backend/src/jobs/limits.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/jobs/offers-purge.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/shopping/offers-purge-readers.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/migrations/tenant/0006_add_flight_search_offers_trimmed_at.sql`, `ota/backend/migrations/README.md`, `packages/db/src/generated/tenant.ts`, `packages/db/src/migrate/baselines.test.ts`, `packages/db/test/integration/baselines.int.test.ts`, `packages/db/test/integration/tenants.int.test.ts`, `packages/testing/test/integration/test-database.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/contract/migration-0002.contract.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/migrations/tenant-0002.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/provisioning/provision.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/dev/dev-seed.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs`, `ota/backend/test/load/README.md`, `ota/docs/adr/0002-offer-and-priced-offer-caching.md`, `ota/docs/data-model.md`, `ota/docs/architecture.md`, `ota/docs/performance.md`, `ota/backend/README.md`, `ota/backend/openapi/README.md`, `docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Added by FIX-W61-PLAN (lead decision (30d) of 2026-11-19, approved by the owner), from OBE-104's finding ([`performance.md`](../performance.md) §11): `offers.purge` keeps an expired search whole while a checkout references one of its priced offers, and no job deletes checkouts, so every checkout, paid or abandoned, keeps all 150 offers of its search (up to 250) for good: 0.34 to 0.48 MiB of `flight_offers` per checkout, about 12 to 17 GiB a year at 100 checkouts a day. The dated revision of OADR-0002 point 6 (decided 2026-11-19, written by FIX-W61-PLAN) says what the purge deletes and keeps; this task applies it and nothing more. Ending the hold of checkouts that never became bookings is not part of it (an option in the ADR's follow-ups that needs a retention period no document sets).
  2. The marker. A tenant migration `0006` (expand) adds the nullable `flight_searches.offers_trimmed_at timestamptz` with its `COMMENT ON`, no backfill: the searches held before it are trimmed by the purge's first runs, oldest first. Add a partial index on `expires_at` for the searches not yet trimmed (`WHERE offers_trimmed_at IS NULL`) only if `EXPLAIN` of either part's choice (step 3) on a schema with thousands of trimmed searches needs one. Regenerate the types (`pnpm db:codegen`), update the tests that list the tenant migrations as `0005` did, and describe the delta in data-model §3 (a new subsection for `0006`) and the purge's row in §6. Code works with schema versions N-1 and N: a tenant whose schema has no marker yet (its migration failed or has not run) keeps today's purge and is not trimmed.
  3. The purge (`offers-purge.processor.ts`): (a) the delete of expired searches that are not held, as today, with `bookings.priced_offer_id` added to the hold and the trimmed searches (marker set) skipped; (b) then the trim of held searches, as the revision says: only searches that have expired, have no unexpired priced offer, have every checkout that holds them final (`completed`, `expired`, `abandoned`) and no marker; the kept rows of items 1 to 5 (the referenced priced offers and the priced offers they were priced from, the offers of their `offer_ids`, each kept upsold offer's upsell and base offer down the chain, the offers a kept offer names in `upsellFlightOfferIds`, the search row); then the priced offers, offers and upsells of the search that are not kept are deleted in an order the foreign keys accept (a non-kept priced offer of a kept offer is deleted by itself, as the cascade from its offer does not reach it), and the marker set, in one transaction per batch. Batches: at most 100 held searches a statement (`JOB_BATCH_LIMITS.searchTrim`), oldest expiry first, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; a full batch of the delete or of the trim asks for a continuation. The job's counts and `offers.purged` add the searches trimmed and the offers, upsells and priced offers deleted by the trim: counts only, never an id. Update the file header with the revised rule.
  4. Unit tests (`offers-purge.processor.test.ts`): the counts and the log line without ids, a continuation after a full batch of either part, a tenant without the marker column purged as before.
  5. Integration tests. `offers-purge.int.test.ts`: each rule of the revision, by the rows left: a search held through each of the three columns; through a priced offer that has not expired; an open checkout that holds the trim back, then trims once it is `expired`; a chain of priced offers (base, ancillary child, re-priced child of the child, a refused re-price and a replaced ancillary child deleted); an upsold offer (its upsell and base offer kept, over two upsells); a priced offer of several offers (`offer_ids`); an offer whose stored answer names `upsellFlightOfferIds`; a trimmed search that the next run reads again in neither part (the marker); a checkout created during a trim, refused by the `RESTRICT` key, and the job's next attempt that keeps it; two tenants, each trimmed in its own schema. `offers-purge-readers.int.test.ts`, through the API, the worker and the Amadeus stub as the existing checkout and booking tests arrange them: read every reader the revision names before a purge and after it, and get the same answer: checkout.get of a completed, an expired and an abandoned checkout (the whole answer compared, for a search result, an upsold offer, a priced offer of several offers and an offer with `upsellOfferIds`); the reconciliation of a lost Create Orders answer (the flights of its e-mail); bookings.cancel's kept fees; bookings.update's contact requirements; flights.getSearch of the trimmed search (`status: "expired"`, its facets, highlights, dictionaries and one-way combinations); the console's booking view (`pricedOfferId`) and supplier log (`searchId`).
  6. Measure with `booking-load.mjs` before (the merge base) and after, one build each, under the soak lock, as OBE-101 measured its bound: two runs of `--tenants 5 --minutes 60` (or a shorter offer lifetime set by the script for both runs alike, said in the report), with a read-only sample every 5 minutes of `flight_offers` and `flight_searches` per tenant schema (rows, size with indexes and TOAST, searches held, trimmed and not yet trimmed) added to the report if it lacks one. Record in performance.md a new section and its §9 row: the rows and MiB of `flight_offers` (and of `flight_searches`) kept per checkout before and after, against §11's 150 rows and 0.34 to 0.48 MiB, the growth per minute of the table once every run's checkout is final, and the purge job's longest run. Update the load README where it describes the samples.
  7. Docs: OADR-0002 (a dated line under point 6's revision: applied by OBE-105, with the measured figures; the Follow-ups' first item done), data-model §3 and §6, architecture.md §6 (the `offers.purge` row), ota/backend/README.md (the purge's paragraph), an errata candidate in ota/backend/openapi/README.md §7 for the frozen db README §6 row on the offer cache purge, and deployment §14 (the `flight_offers` watch: the dated note that OBE-105 is merged and what the table now grows with).
- **Acceptance:**
  - An expired search that no checkout or booking holds, and whose priced offers have expired, is deleted as before. A held search is trimmed once every checkout that holds it is final and none of its priced offers is unexpired: it keeps exactly the rows of OADR-0002 point 6's revision (items 1 to 5), and its other offers, upsells and priced offers are deleted. A search whose checkout is still open, or one of whose priced offers has not expired, is not trimmed; a trimmed search is not read again by later runs; a tenant whose schema has no marker yet is purged as before.
  - Integration tests read every reader the revision names after a purge and get what they got before it (checkout.get of a completed, an expired and an abandoned checkout, compared whole, for a search result, an upsold offer, a priced offer of several offers and an offer with `upsellOfferIds`; the reconciliation's e-mail flights; bookings.cancel's kept fees; bookings.update's contact requirements; flights.getSearch of the trimmed search; the console's booking `pricedOfferId` and supplier log `searchId`); a checkout created during a trim is kept (the `RESTRICT` key and the job's next attempt).
  - `booking-load.mjs` before and after, recorded in performance.md with a §9 row: the rows and MiB of `flight_offers` kept per checkout after the trim, against 150 rows and 0.34 to 0.48 MiB before, and the purge job's longest run; the job logs counts only.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test offers-purge && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int offers-purge && node ota/backend/test/load/booking-load.mjs --tenants 5 --minutes 60`
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decision (30d), approved by the owner, FIX-W61-PLAN):** OBE-105 runs after the launch and keeps its M6 tag: a named exception to the M6 go criterion "every task done", the sixth beside PBE-064, OBE-086, X-042, X-043 and OAD-023 ([roadmap](../../../docs/mvp/plans/roadmap.md) §2.0 and the M6 go/no-go, [ADR-0025](../../../docs/mvp/adr/0025-roadmap-scheduling-and-tracking.md) item 4). Size L: 8 agent-hours, 3.75 developer-hours, 2 solo days, all after the launch, so neither calendar changes length (the roadmap's re-baseline of 2026-11-19). Until it is merged, OADR-0002 point 6 applies as first written, every checkout keeps its search's offers, and the operator watches the size of `flight_offers` monthly ([deployment §14](../../../docs/mvp/deployment-single-vm.md#14-capacity-limits-of-one-vm)); at 100 checkouts a day the 160 GB disk holds years of it. This Note changes no Status.
- **Note (2026-11-19, lead decisions (31c), (31d) and (31e), approved by the owner, FIX-W62-DOCS):** (31c) The tenant migration `0006` of step 2 (the nullable `flight_searches.offers_trimmed_at` marker, no backfill) is accepted as a schema delta over the frozen reference SQL, which this task documents in data-model §3 as the deltas of `0002` to `0005` are documented. (31d) After a trim, the deleted offers and priced offers of a held search answer `404` instead of `410 OFFER_EXPIRED` on flights.getOffer, flights.price, flights.upsell, flights.getPricedOffer and checkout.create, as for the searches the purge deletes whole, and a trimmed search's highlights and one-way combinations may name deleted offers: accepted as is, so this task does not keep the offers the highlights name. (31e) No retention period is set now for checkouts that never became bookings: this task's trim bounds the growth, and that option stays in OADR-0002's Follow-ups, to revisit after the launch with real volumes. This Note changes no Status and no estimate.

## M7 — Multi-supplier engine

The supplier ingestion engine with its adapters (Amadeus, PKFare), the platform registry with the supplier switches, the hidden supplier, the rules at the hooks and the reconciliation role. The owner decided on 2026-11-25 that M7 is built before the launch ([ADR-0030](../../../docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md) items 19 to 25; [ADR-0025](../../../docs/mvp/adr/0025-roadmap-scheduling-and-tracking.md) item 3, revision of 2026-11-25). The design is in the [multi-supplier plan](../../../docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md). Each block names the plan task it comes from ("plan key") and the record items it builds. A record item that is still marked **Proposed** is accepted when the owner starts the wave of a task that names it (ADR-0030 item 26). Every task also keeps the guidebook current, as the definition of done in AGENTS.md asks; plan-lint does not accept `guidebook/` paths in Files, so the blocks do not list them, and a block that moves or renames something the guidebook cites names the update in its steps. Tasks that add a migration take the next free number; when two of them run in parallel, the wave integrator renumbers the later one at merge, with the tests that list the migrations. Seven tasks were added in the review of 2026-11-25 (PBE-105, PAD-025 and X-075 in M7; OBE-215, PBE-106, OBE-216 and PBE-107 in M8); they have no plan key. Tests written after X-075 write the platform's supplier rows (connections and supply sources) only through X-075's builders. The blocks cite the lead's rulings for the task blocks by their codes (G1 to G12, T, and S1 to S18); [Annex D of the plan](../../../docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md#annex-d-the-leads-rulings-for-the-task-blocks) states each one, and a ruling that makes a design choice is a proposal of the lead (ADR-0030 item 26).

- **Note (2026-11-25):** This task builds none of the Proposed record items its Read first names. It reads OADR-0020 items 4 to 13 only for the PKFare facts they rest on. Under ADR-0030 item 26 (proposed) a block names in Read first the record items it builds, so the lead lists none of items 4 to 13 for this task when its wave is proposed, and the owner's go for that wave does not accept them on this task's account.
- **Note (2026-11-27, the owner's PKFare documentation):** On 2026-11-27 the owner committed PKFare's Flight Buyer API pages as `docs/pkfare/` (commit 4f740863; 146 pages downloaded from open.pkfare.com that day, indexed by `docs/pkfare/README.md`) and wrote: "I have added the pkfare documentation to "docs/pkfare". Relevant APIs for booking flow are :- Shopping, PrecisePricing, ancillaryPricing, preciseBooking, cancelOrder, orderPricing, OrderDetail, TicketIssuanceNotify. The workflow can be seen in https://apifox.pkfare.com/static-upload/doc-image/custom/20241129/51d41639-369d-47e9-aacb-279a229bf0f8.png. Go through it, keep a note (maybe a starter task) and then start working on wave 71." The lead reads this as follows. The human step of step 1 is done, inside the repository, so step 2's "The pages are not committed" and the index `docs/pkfare-api/README.md` no longer describe the saved reference. The note is kept on this task, not in a new starter task, because this task has no dependency and already owns the facts file and the question list. Proposed (lead), made after the owner's go for wave 71 and named in the wave's report, where the owner may change it:
  - Files drop `docs/pkfare-api/README.md`. `docs/pkfare/README.md` is the index of step 2. This task reads `docs/pkfare/` and never edits it.
  - Acceptance 2 reads "Every `stated` row cites a page of `docs/pkfare/` by path and line, and every `assumed` row has a question". Acceptance 3 reads "`docs/pkfare-api/` does not exist, and the facts file holds no partner id, key, signature, passcode or personal data".
  - The Verify becomes `test -f ota/docs/suppliers/pkfare-facts.md && test -f docs/pkfare/README.md && test ! -e docs/pkfare-api && grep -cE '(stated|observed|assumed)' ota/docs/suppliers/pkfare-facts.md`.
  - Step 6 adds `docs/pkfare/` to §7 of `docs/mvp/README.md`, beside `docs/amadeus-api/`.
  - The workflow image is not among the pages. A fact that only the image gives is `assumed`, names the image as its source and gets a question; `stated` stays for the pages (step 4).
  - Ticketing and Penalty are not in the owner's list. The image names both, and Ticketing is the call that pays, so the facts file keeps both.
  - Size M may not hold for 146 pages; the lead may resize this task to L.

  Whether PKFare's terms allow the pages in the repository (A42), and whether `docs/pkfare/` joins the reference material of `docs/mvp/decisions.md` §3 and the pull-request guard of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, are for the owner (ADR-0030 question 22); this note decides neither. The pages hold sample partner ids and signs, a sample Signature V2 secret, sample mailbox passcodes, sample traveller and contact data, and the names and addresses of PKFare staff. The facts file copies none of them.
- **Note (2026-11-27, PKFare's flow and its time limits):** The image is PKFare's "API Interaction Workflow"; its address carries 20241129. As the lead transcribed it:
  - Search Flights: Shopping_V4 Json; "miniRules only for reference"; "Cache/Responding time".
  - 30 mins, then Select Flights: precisePricing_V6 Json and Penalty; "IF Pricing failed then direct Pricing again"; optional "Add an Ancillary" with ancillaryPricing V5 Json.
  - 30 mins, then Create an order: precisePricing_V6 Json and preciseBooking_V5 Json; cancelOrder Json for "Cancel unpaid order" and "In case of duplicate booking".
  - 60 mins, then Payment: orderPricing_V4 Json and Ticketing Json.
  - Issuance: TicketIssuanceNotify V2 and orderDetail_V9 Json.

  The image adds PKFare's note that the airline's own reference (airPNR) is known only once the ticket is issued, and that the airline may change it while issuing. The pages give the same order of calls (`docs/pkfare/Docs/Guides/Book air tickets with ancillaries.md`) and state these limits: PreciseBooking within 30 minutes of PrecisePricing; AncillaryPricing results valid for half an hour; Ticketing within 30 minutes of OrderPricing, which the image does not show; and a ticketing deadline `lastTktTime` per flight, with OrderPricing refusing B026 within one hour of it. The image's 30 minutes from search to selection and 60 minutes from order to payment are on the image only, and their meaning is `assumed`. Of the owner's eight APIs, TicketIssuanceNotify is the one call PKFare makes to us: a POST to a URL we give PKFare, received by OBE-182. PKFare pushes other notices too, such as ScheduleChangeNotify.
- **Note (2026-11-27, facts that later blocks do not yet assume):** The lead's first read of the pages found the facts below. This task records each as a row with its page and line. The lead writes dated notes on the named blocks before their wave, and each block still reads the facts file first.
  - Besides the fixed MD5 `sign`, PKFare is introducing Signature V2: an HMAC-SHA256 in `X-PK-*` headers. PKFare's account manager sets the mode per Partner ID, and Legacy is the default for existing buyers; Velexis's mode is `assumed`. OBE-159, PBE-079, PBE-083, PBE-084, X-056 and X-058.
  - PrecisePricing returns no price-validity time: its `latestTktTime` is a ticketing deadline. It can refuse with B026. On B020 or B021 PKFare advises one retry with solutionId "direct pricing", whose answer is a new offer. OBE-162. Penalty is suggested 10 seconds after PrecisePricing. OBE-164.
  - Booking codes: B005 also follows changed parameters or concurrent calls; B006 carries an order number; B008 is never retried; B012 and B028 are time-outs after which an order may exist; B017 means the price changed; B029 is a duplicate, and PKFare can be set to return the earlier order number; B087 is churning. OBE-169.
  - OrderPricing right after booking can fail with B103, B107 or B109, and PKFare advises a retry or two minutes' wait; B107 and B109 also say the fare changed, and B112 says the order was already paid. Its answer has no total, and PKFare quotes net fares only. Ticketing's schema types `orderAmount` as an integer while its sample has decimals. OBE-108, OBE-165, OBE-170 and OBE-172.
  - Statuses: HOLD and UNDER_REVIEW are not final, CNCL_TO_BE_REIM ends in CNCL_REIMED, and RSV_FAIL is final. RequestTicketing reminds PKFare of an issuing order, once per 10 minutes. OBE-173.
  - An order can hold several airline references, joined by "|", and a traveller several ticket numbers, joined by "/"; OBE-174's acceptance has one ticket row per traveller. In PKFare's samples for two low-cost carriers `ticketNum` equals the airline's reference, and a how-to page advises checking for 13 digits; whether that is the rule is `assumed`. OBE-154, OBE-174 and OBE-181.
  - The low-cost mark: PKFare's airline list marks each carrier LCC or FSC, and Shopping V10 can filter by a ContentSource tag, which Shopping_V4 lacks. OBE-161 and OADR-0020 question 1.
  - PrecisePricing's `ancillaryAvailability` says whether paid bags and seats exist. OBE-180.
  - The push: `buyerOrder` is in its schema but in neither sample, OrderDetail has no such field, and PreciseBooking gives it no length. Its body holds passport numbers and birthdays. Our answer body is fixed; an older push page says PKFare tries again four times otherwise. X-056's recorder cannot record a push. OBE-182 and X-057.
  - OrderDetail's check-in data and CheckInInfoPush can carry a booking mailbox and its passcode, which are never stored or logged; OrderDetail can be asked without them. OBE-174.
  - Fixtures: in the sandbox only, ModifyOrderStatus moves a paid order to ISSED; AK, UO and TG are PKFare's test airlines; P008 refuses fake names such as TEST. X-056 and X-057.
- **Note (2026-11-27, API versions):** The image names PKFare's set of 2024: Shopping_V4, precisePricing_V6, ancillaryPricing V5, preciseBooking_V5, orderPricing_V4, orderDetail_V9 and TicketIssuanceNotify V2. The pages' release of 2026/08/13 is newer: Shopping V10, PrecisePricing V12, PreciseBooking V8, AncillaryPricing V7, Penalty V4, OrderPricing V6 and OrderDetail V14; TicketIssuanceNotify_V3 is newer than V2 and undated. CancelOrder and Ticketing have one JSON version each. The pages have no JSON page for Shopping_V4 or precisePricing_V6, only rows in version tables, and PKFare's UAT guide requires the latest version unless PKFare confirms an exception. The facts file states both sets per operation, and "Questions for PKFare" asks which set Velexis certifies on. Which set the build uses is ADR-0030 question 21, with the lead's recommendation: ask PKFare first, and build on the newest set unless PKFare grants the image's set in writing. This task does not need the answer; OBE-159 and the tasks after it do.
- **Note (2026-11-27, corrections to the notes above):** A check of the three notes above against the pages, and this task's facts file (`ota/docs/suppliers/pkfare-facts.md`, which cites each fact by page and line), correct them as follows. Where a note and the facts file differ, the facts file holds.
  - Ticketing's JSON page types `orderAmount` as an integer, and its example is 2015; `payAmount` and `transactionExpense` carry decimals there, and the legacy Ticketing page types all three as BigDecimal. So amounts are read as decimals.
  - B012 and B028 are time-outs. The pages do not say whether an order exists after them; that is `assumed` and a question for PKFare. Of the two forms of B006, one says an order was created and gives its number; where that number sits in the JSON answer is `assumed`.
  - PKFare's note on PNR and airPNR is on the pages too (`Docs/Guides/Book air tickets with ancillaries.md`), so it is `stated`: for low-cost and NDC content the PNR is PKFare's own reference, and the airline's reference comes with issuance and may change while issuing. OrderDetail V14 gives it at ISSED, though one of its ISS_PRC examples shows one.
  - The "direct pricing" retry is a fallback, not the default flow, and works from PrecisePricing V6 on. PKFare recommends AK, UO and TG for tests. That a booking mailbox passcode is never stored or logged is Velexis's rule (CLAUDE.md rule 5), not PKFare's. The older TicketingNumPush_V2 example does carry `buyerOrder`; the TicketIssuanceNotify_V3 examples do not.
  - preciseBooking_V5 has no JSON page either. The newest set includes Penalty V4. The release note dates five of the image's seven versions to 2024; it gives no date for the JSON Shopping_V4 or orderDetail_V9.
  - The notes left out facts that the facts file holds and later blocks need: PKFare advises polling OrderDetail every 5 to 10 minutes beside the push (OBE-173). A code can mean different things in different calls: B022 is a child's age in PreciseBooking but a short balance in Ticketing, and B024 a time-out in PrecisePricing but an order already paid in Ticketing, so X-057's B022 and B024 are Ticketing's (OBE-169, OBE-172, X-057). Under Signature V2 the body is signed as sent and never serialised again or compressed, every request and retry gets a new timestamp, request id and signature, and neither the secret nor `X-PK-Signature` is logged (OBE-159, PBE-083). `solutionId` is opaque and stored whole (OBE-161, OBE-162). WalletBalance and RequestTicketing are in the facts file too, though neither the owner's list nor the image names them.
  - The facts file also says which facts of plan §9.2 the pages answer, for example: OrderDetail finds an order only by PKFare's order number, not by our reference; a sub-buyer's wallet is separate from the main buyer's or shared with it; and PKFare gives the production host after testing.
- **Note (2026-11-27, merged):** done in wave 71 (docs(ota): write the PKFare facts file and its questions for PKFare [OBE-107]), as the notes of 2026-11-27 re-scope it: no `docs/pkfare-api/`, and `docs/pkfare/README.md` is the index. The facts file holds 124 facts (87 `stated`, 37 `assumed`, none `observed` yet), the API versions of the image and of the pages, and 37 questions for PKFare. Which version set the build uses stays ADR-0030 question 21, and whether `docs/pkfare/` joins `decisions.md` §3 stays question 22.

### OBE-109 · Record a golden baseline of today's Amadeus search, pricing and upsell ✅
- **Status:** done (branch claude/intelligent-bardeen-90hhu7)
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** —

- **Files:** `ota/backend/test/integration/supply/golden-shopping.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/supply/golden/`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. List the stub scenarios that the three shopping integration files run for `flights.search`, `flights.price` and `flights.upsell`: the success fixtures and each refusal. The golden test runs them through the API in-process, with the same set-up.

The stub's `requests()` holds no body: take the bodies from a spy on `globalThis.fetch` that passes every call through. Leave out the token request, whose body holds the client secret.
  3. Store the records as files under `ota/backend/test/supply/golden/`, in a form that `pnpm format:check` accepts. One helper replaces only what differs from run to run (generated ids, timestamps, durations, request ids) by fixed placeholders. Amadeus request bodies are compared byte for byte.

  5. Prove that the test bites: change one character of a request that `buildAmadeusSearch` builds, see it fail, revert, and say so in the pull request.
  6. README §8: what the baseline holds, how to record it again, and that a golden file changes only in a task whose block names the difference.
- **Acceptance:**
  - `golden-shopping.int.test.ts` passes on today's code and holds, per scenario, the Amadeus request bodies, the `supplier_requests` rows, the stored offer and priced-offer rows and the API answers of search, price and upsell.
  - A one-byte change of a request body fails the test.
  - No file under `ota/backend/src` and no existing test changes.
  - The golden files hold no token, secret or card number, and no token request.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int golden-shopping`
- **Note (2026-11-27, merged):** done in wave 71 (test(ota-backend): record a golden baseline of today's Amadeus search, pricing and upsell [OBE-109]): 40 scenarios under `ota/backend/test/supply/golden/`.   - The neutral offer carries a supplier offer reference; no exported name contains a supplier's name.

  4. `capabilities()` returns the declaration of a source's adapter. Start the Amadeus adapter class with its declaration only: one value per row of plan §4.2 that describes today's behaviour. The pull request names the code behind each value.
  5. `supply.module.ts` provides the registry; no business module uses it yet.
  6. Unit tests with the fake adapter and a fake platform read: an `active` row gives one source; no row or another status gives none, with the reason; a row of another tenant or environment never serves; an unknown supplier fails.
- **Acceptance:**
  - The registry returns the Amadeus source exactly when the connection that the resolver reads is `active`, and it reads through `PlatformCache` only.
  - Look-up returns the registered adapter, an unknown supplier fails, and the Amadeus declaration has a value for every row of plan §4.2.
  - No caller changes: the golden test of OBE-109 passes.

### OBE-114 · Build the engine core: the action pipeline, the three hooks and routing by row
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** OBE-112, OBE-110, OBE-109
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md §4.1 and §4.3 (plan key E2-07; the action table, the hook table and its last bullet); docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md (items 13 and 20; item 16, proposed); ota/docs/adr/0019-supplier-ingestion-engine-and-adapters.md (items 3 and 4; item 8, proposed; item 11, proposed; item 12, proposed; item 14, proposed); ota/backend/src/supply/interface/; ota/backend/src/supply/registry/; ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts; ota/backend/src/bookings/staff-alerts.ts (`StaffAlerts`, which reach OTA staff); the block of X-072 (the alert inventory)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/supply/engine/`, `ota/backend/src/supply/supply.module.ts`, `ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts`, `ota/backend/README.md`, `ota/docs/architecture.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. One pipeline for every action of plan §4.1: pre-action hooks, the adapter step, post-action hooks once per supplier result and, for Search, post-merge hooks once on the merged list. One table in code drives it: per action, its outcome set and its hook policy (the column "Hooks" of §4.1 and the last bullet of §4.3). The engine answers outcomes only.
  2. Routing: Search goes to every source of the registry. Any other action takes the source that its caller read from the offer or booking row; a row without a source, or with an unknown one, is refused before any adapter step (`unknown-source-refused`).
  3. Hook inputs are typed as the hook table of §4.3 says, and the engine checks each result against its row. Pre-action may remove a source or refuse; it never adds a source or changes travellers, dates or amounts. Post-action may drop offers or adjust a price, on Search and Price only (an upsell takes the hooks of Price, OBE-121); it never changes flights. Post-merge never changes a price.
  4. On money and servicing actions the hooks get read-only inputs, and nothing they return is applied (`money-hooks-cannot-mutate`); on Create order, pre-action may refuse.
  5. A hook that throws fails Search, Price and Create order closed (`hook-failure-fails-closed`). On the six other actions the action goes on (`hook-failure-never-blocks-servicing`), and the failure is the alert of plan §4.3: one error log event `supply.hook_failed` with the hook, the action and the source, without payload, secret or personal data. It reaches Velexis staff through the alert inventory of X-072, never through `StaffAlerts`, which reach OTA staff and would reveal Velexis's rules.
  6. Register no handler, so no request changes. Handlers are code: nothing from a tenant or from staff is stored or run.
  7. Unit tests under these four names, with the fake adapter, which also supplies the step of an action without an adapter method.
- **Acceptance:**
  - The tests `unknown-source-refused`, `money-hooks-cannot-mutate`, `hook-failure-fails-closed` and `hook-failure-never-blocks-servicing` pass with the fake; the last two cover every action of plan §4.1.
  - A pre-action hook cannot add a source, a post-action hook cannot change flights, and a post-merge hook cannot change a price.
  - A hook that fails on a servicing action writes one `supply.hook_failed` event, without payload, and no staff alert of the OTA.
  - Nothing calls the engine yet: the golden test of OBE-109 passes.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test supply/engine && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int golden-shopping`
- **Note (2026-11-25):** OBE-109 and OBE-110 are added as dependencies: the acceptance runs OBE-109's golden test, and this task builds on OBE-110's interface and extends its fake adapter. The event of step 5 and its receiver are the lead's ruling S12: X-072's inventory names the event with its receiver and runbook, and its drill raises it.
- **Note (2026-11-25):** Rests on ADR-0030, question (44c): the hooks keep the names "pre-action", "post-action" and "post-merge" until the owner answers. The wave proposal names it; the owner's go for the wave accepts it.
- **Note (2026-11-26):** Question (44c) was answered on 2026-11-26: the hooks keep their names (ADR-0030 item 29; OADR-0019 item 16). The lead reads the owner's sentence as agreeing with the hook policy of step 1 where it speaks: Search may have all three hooks, and a booking action has no post-merge hook. The rest of that policy (Price and extras pre-action and post-action; Create order only a pre-action point that may refuse; the other actions only observe, or have no hook) stays as the block has it. Whether "nothing would be bound here" also rules out that point on Create order is ADR-0030 question 17; until it is answered, step 4 stands, and this task binds no handler (step 6).

### OBE-116 · Merge search results with a share of the limit per source and one currency
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** OBE-115, OBE-110, OBE-112, OBE-113, OBE-114, OBE-109
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md §3, §4.1, §4.3 and §7 (plan key E2-09; A17; in §7 the row "Rules for shares, deadlines, preferred source"); docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md (item 13); ota/docs/adr/0019-supplier-ingestion-engine-and-adapters.md (item 3; item 8, proposed; item 11, proposed); ota/backend/src/shopping/offers.mapper.ts (`MAX_OFFERS_PER_SEARCH`, `offersBoundOf`); ota/backend/src/shopping/searches.service.ts (`complete`)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/supply/engine/`, `ota/backend/src/shopping/searches.service.ts`, `ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts`, `ota/docs/flows/search-and-price.md`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Write the merge as a pure function of the engine, run at post-merge. Input: each source's offers in the order of its answer, and the limit. Output: the kept offers and the counts kept and dropped per source.
  2. The limit is today's: what the search asks for (`max` or `maxFlightOffers`, bounded by `offersBoundOf`), never above `MAX_OFFERS_PER_SEARCH`.
  3. Shares are equal by default: the limit divided among the sources that answered, the remainder to the first in the registry's order. A source with fewer offers than its share passes the rest on. Inside a source the order of its answer decides.
  4. The shares are a typed settings object of the engine with defaults in code: no table, no API member, no environment variable. OBE-193 puts stored rules behind it.
  5. One currency per search, no conversion. A source whose declared currencies lack the search's currency is not called: `skipped`, with the reason stored. An offer in another currency is dropped and counted.
  6. `SearchesService.complete` stores the merged list; `flight_search_sources` gets the offers received, kept and dropped.
  7. Unit tests with two fake sources: equal shares; an odd limit; a short, an empty and a failed source; three sources; a source skipped for the currency; one source alone.
- **Acceptance:**
  - With one source the merged list is the source's list cut at today's limit: `search.int.test.ts` and the golden test of OBE-109 pass unchanged.
  - With two fake sources each gets half of the limit, an unused share passes to the other, and the list never exceeds the limit.
  - A source that cannot quote the search's currency gets no call and a stored skip reason; no amount is converted.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test supply/engine && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int shopping golden-shopping`
- **Note (2026-11-25):** The settings object of step 4 with its defaults in code is Proposed (lead); confirm in the pull request. Added dependencies, whose products this task uses: OBE-110 (the fake adapter), OBE-112 (the registry's order), OBE-113 (`flight_search_sources`), OBE-114 (the post-merge hook) and OBE-109 (the golden test of the acceptance).

### OBE-117 · Remove like-for-like duplicates across sources at post-merge
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** OBE-116, OBE-110, OBE-112, OBE-114, OBE-109
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md §2, §3, §4.1 and §4.3 (plan key E2-10; the lead's proposal 3, not confirmed; A17 and A18); docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md (item 13); ota/docs/adr/0019-supplier-ingestion-engine-and-adapters.md (item 3; item 8, proposed; item 11, proposed); ota/backend/src/supply/engine/
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/supply/engine/`, `ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts`, `ota/docs/flows/search-and-price.md`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. The like-for-like key is a pure function of a neutral offer. It holds what A18 compares: every segment's flight (carrier, number, airports, local times) and cabin, the included checked bags, and the change and refund conditions; not the price. An offer with an unknown change or refund condition is like no other offer, so both stay.
  2. Removal runs at post-merge, before the shares and the limit (the order of plan §4.3). Among offers of different sources with one key, one stays.
  3. Two settings decide the winner: a preferred source and a minimum saving. The other source's offer wins only when it is cheaper than the preferred source's by at least the minimum saving. The price compared is the offer's total at post-merge.
  4. Both join the settings object of OBE-116, with neutral defaults: no preferred source and a minimum saving of 0. Then the cheaper offer wins, and a tie keeps the first source in the registry's order. The owner's numbers are not decided.
  5. A losing duplicate is not stored (A17) and counts as dropped for its source.
  6. Unit tests with two fake sources: equal flights, cabins, bags and conditions; a different cabin, bag allowance or condition; cheaper below and above the minimum saving; no preferred source; a tie; an unknown condition.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Two like-for-like offers of two fake sources give one stored offer; offers that differ in flights, cabin, included bags or a change or refund condition both stay.
  - With a preferred source and a minimum saving, the other source wins only when it is cheaper by at least that saving; the losing offer is not stored and counts as dropped.
  - With one source nothing is removed: `search.int.test.ts` and the golden test of OBE-109 pass unchanged.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test supply/engine && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int shopping golden-shopping`
- **Note (2026-11-25):** Proposed (lead); confirm in the pull request: the settings with their defaults (no preferred source, a minimum saving of 0), an unknown condition never a duplicate, and the total compared at post-merge. Added dependencies, whose products this task uses: OBE-110 (the fake adapter), OBE-112 (the registry's order), OBE-114 (the post-merge hook) and OBE-109 (the golden test of the acceptance).

### OBE-122 · Add the adapter conformance suite, part 1, for the Amadeus adapter and the fake
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** OBE-120, OBE-110, OBE-112, OBE-115, OBE-118, OBE-119, OBE-111
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md §4.1, §4.2 and §4.15 (plan key E2-15); docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md (items 1, 4 and 13); ota/docs/adr/0019-supplier-ingestion-engine-and-adapters.md (items 1 and 2; item 8, proposed; item 9, proposed); ota/docs/adr/0001-amadeus-client-design.md (points 7 and 9); ota/backend/src/supply/interface/; ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts; tools/amadeus-stub/README.md (the scenarios `timeout`, `server-error`, `sold-out`, `price-changed`; the `timers` option)
- **Files:** `ota/backend/test/supply/conformance/`, `ota/backend/test/integration/supply/conformance-amadeus.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/supply/conformance-fake.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. The suite is one function in `ota/backend/test/supply/conformance/` that takes a harness (build the adapter, make its supplier answer a scenario, read its call-log rows). Each adapter has one small test file that calls it. OBE-140 adds part 2; OBE-166 runs it for PKFare.
  2. Capabilities: a value for every capability of the declaration (the rows of plan §4.2 and those added later, such as upsell); the adapter does nothing that it declares missing.
  3. Search and read: `prepare` is pure. A search answers one of `ok`, `empty`, `failed`, `timed_out` or `skipped`; every offer is a neutral offer with a supplier offer reference, and an unreadable offer is counted. The readers read back what the adapter stored and refuse another supplier's data.
  4. Price: a scenario produces each of `priced`, `sold_out`, `refused` and `unavailable`, and no other outcome.
  5. Deadlines: an answer held past the source's deadline gives `timed_out` for Search and `unavailable` for Price, and the call is aborted.
  6. Redaction: a known secret, token and contact value of the scenario are in no call-log row, log line or error; no key, signature, card number or document number is stored.
  7. No supplier name in neutral output: outside the stored payload that only the adapter's reader opens, outcomes, offers, priced offers and errors hold no supplier name, error code or payload.
  8. A broken fake fails the matching case (a leaked name, a late answer, an outcome outside the set, an unredacted secret). README §8 says how a new adapter joins.
- **Acceptance:**
  - The same cases run against the Amadeus adapter with its stub and against the fake: capabilities, search, read, price, deadlines, redaction, no supplier name in neutral output.
  - A broken fake fails the matching case, and the suite takes a harness, so OBE-140 and OBE-166 copy no case.
  - No file under `ota/backend/src` and no existing test changes.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int supply/conformance`
- **Note (2026-11-25):** Added dependencies, whose products this task uses: OBE-115 (the adapter's search and its deadline, which no other dependency brings), OBE-110 (the interface and the fake), OBE-112 (the declaration), OBE-118 and OBE-119 (the readers) and OBE-111 (the common call log, whose rows the harness reads). The critical path keeps its length.

The stub's `requests()` holds no body, so the test takes each request (method, path, query and body) from a spy on `globalThis.fetch` that passes every call through, as OBE-109 does; `AMADEUS_FETCH` calls it at call time. ### OBE-139 · Add the optional service request and notification operations to the interface and the engine
- **Status:** todo
- **Component:** ota-backend
- **Milestone:** M7
- **Depends on:** OBE-134, OBE-110, OBE-114
- **Size:** M
- **Read first:** docs/mvp/plans/multi-supplier-plan.md §4.1, §4.10 and §4.12 (plan key E3-16; the row "Service request"; the bullet "PKFare's notifications are not authenticated"); docs/mvp/adr/0030-suppliers-supply-sources-and-ingestion-engine.md (items 1 and 4); ota/docs/adr/0019-supplier-ingestion-engine-and-adapters.md (item 2; item 8, proposed; item 9, proposed; item 14, proposed); ota/backend/src/supply/engine/ (the action table of OBE-114); the block of OBE-182
- **Files:** `ota/backend/src/supply/interface/`, `ota/backend/src/supply/engine/`, `ota/backend/src/supply/adapters/amadeus/`, `ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts`, `ota/backend/README.md`, `ota/docs/architecture.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Service request: an optional adapter method for the kinds void, refund and change, with the outcomes `quoted`, `submitted`, `completed` and `refused` (plan §4.1). The capability "Cancel, void, refund, change" says whether a source serves a kind by API, by request or not at all. The engine routes by the booking's source and never calls an adapter that does not declare the kind. Hooks observe only: a failing hook gives the event `supply.hook_failed` of OBE-114, and the request goes on.
  2. Notification: an optional adapter method that reads an inbound supplier message into a neutral trigger: which order it names, and nothing else. The engine's only reaction is Read order (OBE-134) for that booking. It never changes a booking, a payment or a ticket from the message's content (`notification-triggers-read-only`).
  3. A message that names no known booking is dropped and counted. The message is not stored; a log line holds counts and ids only.
  4. The Amadeus adapter declares neither. No business code calls them yet; the endpoint for notifications is OBE-182.
  5. Unit tests with the fake: `notification-triggers-read-only` (a message that claims a ticket or an amount leads to one Read order and to no other write); each outcome of a service request.
  6. Describe both operations in README §2 and architecture.md §2.
- **Acceptance:**
  - The interface and the engine have the optional service request (void, refund, change; `quoted`, `submitted`, `completed`, `refused`) and the notification; the Amadeus adapter declares none.
  - The test `notification-triggers-read-only` passes with the fake: a notification leads to at most one Read order and to no other write, whatever it claims.
  - An adapter that declares no service request is never called, and a failing hook does not stop one. No file of `ota/backend/src` outside `src/supply/` changes.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test supply && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend typecheck`
- **Note (2026-11-25):** OBE-110 and OBE-114 are added as dependencies: the interface with the fake, and the engine with its action table.

- **Files:** `ota/backend/test/supply/conformance/`, `ota/backend/test/integration/supply/conformance-amadeus.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/integration/supply/conformance-fake.int.test.ts`, `ota/backend/test/supply/fake-adapter.ts`, `ota/backend/README.md`
- **Steps:**
  1. Extend the harness of OBE-122: both test files run part 2 beside part 1. A case runs only for an adapter that declares its capability.
  2. Create order: a scenario for each of `created`, `rejected`, `not_sent` and `unknown`, and no other outcome. `create-order-lost-answer`: the supplier creates the order and the answer is lost; the adapter answers `unknown`, never `rejected` or `not_sent`, and sends no second request.

  7. The suite's own test: a broken fake fails the matching case (`rejected` on a lost answer, `absent` on an incomplete search, a second ticketing request, an unredacted snapshot).
- **Acceptance:**
  - Part 2 runs against the Amadeus adapter with its stub and against the fake: the four create outcomes with `create-order-lost-answer`, `find-order-incomplete-never-absent`, ticketing now and later, read, cancel, service requests, notifications and the redaction of the order snapshot.
  - A broken fake fails the matching case, and OBE-184 can run part 2 for another adapter without copying a case.
  - No file under `ota/backend/src` and no existing test changes.

- **Note (2026-11-25):** OBE-110 and OBE-122 are added as dependencies: the fake and the harness of part 1.

- **Steps:**
  1. The recorder gets an option for an order of a source that tickets later; the ticketing capability decides it, never a supplier's name (A34).
  2. With the option, the record step writes the booking and its children as today, but queues no `booking.confirmed` e-mail and writes no customer-visible event "confirmed by the airline" (the summary of `booking.created`).

The other sentences stay as they are at the merge base, and the `manual_review` sentence keeps "Our team will issue your e-tickets", which `booking-orchestrator.service.test.ts` pins. The problem sentences for `failed` and `manual_review` are OBE-156's, and the sentence for a ticketless booking is OBE-186's: whichever of OBE-143, OBE-156 and OBE-186 merges last keeps every change, and the pinned "Our team will issue your e-tickets" holds.
  6. Tests: `held-confirmation.int.test.ts` for both entries, the second also called twice; unit tests of `ticketingMessageOf`.
- **Acceptance:**
  - With the option, the record step queues no `booking.confirmed` e-mail and writes no customer-visible confirmation event; the second entry writes both exactly once.
  - `ticketingMessageOf` answers "We are finalising your booking" while the confirmation is held back and keeps its other sentences, "Our team will issue your e-tickets" included.
  - Without the option the recorder behaves as before: the nine booking integration files pass unchanged. No test is deleted or weakened.
- **Verify:** `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test order-recorder booking-orchestrator bookings.mapper && pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-backend test:int bookings held-confirmation`

OBE-156 and OBE-186 also change `ticketingMessageOf`: whichever of OBE-143, OBE-156 and OBE-186 merges last keeps every change; the pinned "Our team will issue your e-tickets" holds.
